item.content:encoded:
The 2027 Entrepreneurs for Resilience (E4R) programme is inviting innovative social enterprises to apply for an opportunity designed to help scale solutions that improve access to affordable, high-quality primary healthcare for underserved communities in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).

Organised by the Swiss Re Foundation, the 2027 edition represents a significant milestone as the programme enters its 10th edition, marking a decade of supporting innovative social enterprises working to build more resilient communities.

For this special 10th-anniversary edition, Entrepreneurs for Resilience is turning its attention to one of the most persistent challenges facing underserved populations around the world: limited access to quality and affordable primary healthcare.

The programme is particularly interested in social enterprises that are developing innovative brick-and-click healthcare models. These models combine physical, community-based healthcare solutions with digital technologies to make healthcare services more accessible, affordable and convenient.

Successful entrepreneurs will have the opportunity to receive a combination of funding, tailored advisory support, corporate expertise, professional networks and peer-to-peer learning. The goal is to help participating enterprises strengthen their business and impact models, expand their reach and ultimately enable more people to access the healthcare services they need.

About the Entrepreneurs for Resilience Programme

Entrepreneurs for Resilience is an initiative of the Swiss Re Foundation that supports social entrepreneurs developing innovative solutions to major resilience challenges.

Over the years, the programme has worked with entrepreneurs seeking to address complex social and environmental challenges while developing sustainable business models capable of creating measurable impact.

The 2027 edition is particularly important because it marks the 10th edition of Entrepreneurs for Resilience. The milestone provides an opportunity to continue the programme’s focus on supporting innovative enterprises while addressing a critical issue affecting millions of people: access to primary healthcare.

For communities that are underserved by conventional healthcare systems, social enterprises can play an important role by developing alternative approaches that combine entrepreneurship, technology, community engagement and healthcare delivery.

What Is the Focus of Entrepreneurs for Resilience 2027?

The 2027 programme focuses specifically on scaling access to affordable, quality primary healthcare for underserved populations in low- and middle-income countries.

Primary healthcare is often the first point of contact between individuals and the health system. However, many communities continue to experience barriers that make accessing essential healthcare difficult.

According to the programme description, some of the major barriers include:

  • High costs, which can prevent individuals and families from seeking essential healthcare.
  • Distance, particularly for people living in remote or underserved communities.
  • Limited availability of quality services, which can leave communities without reliable healthcare options.
  • Access challenges, where conventional healthcare infrastructure may not adequately serve the needs of certain populations.

The E4R 2027 programme is therefore looking for entrepreneurs whose solutions can help overcome these barriers and bring healthcare services closer to the people who need them.

What Are “Brick-and-Click” Healthcare Models?

One of the defining features of the 2027 Entrepreneurs for Resilience programme is its focus on brick-and-click healthcare models.

A brick-and-click model combines physical and digital healthcare solutions.

The “brick” component can refer to physical healthcare infrastructure or services, such as

  • Clinics
  • Community healthcare centres
  • Pharmacies
  • Diagnostic facilities
  • Healthcare delivery points
  • Community-based health services

The “click” component can involve digital technologies and platforms, such as

  • Telemedicine
  • Digital health platforms
  • Online consultations
  • Mobile health applications
  • Digital appointment systems
  • Remote diagnostics
  • Digital patient-management systems
  • Technology-enabled healthcare access

By combining physical and digital approaches, these models can potentially address different barriers to healthcare access simultaneously.

For example, a social enterprise could operate physical healthcare facilities within underserved communities while using digital technology to provide remote consultations, manage appointments, facilitate follow-up care or connect patients with healthcare professionals.

The programme is particularly interested in entrepreneurs using this type of integrated approach to bring quality healthcare closer to underserved populations.

What Support Will Selected Entrepreneurs Receive?

Selected entrepreneurs will receive a combination of financial and non-financial support intended to help them strengthen and scale their enterprises.

1. Funding

Selected social enterprises will receive funding to support their efforts to strengthen and expand their solutions.

Financial support can be particularly important for social enterprises seeking to move from an established model to a larger scale of operations.

2. Tailored Advisory Support

Participants will benefit from tailored advisory support designed around their needs.

This can help entrepreneurs identify opportunities to strengthen their business models, improve their operations and develop strategies for sustainable growth and impact.

3. Access to Corporate Expertise

The programme provides access to corporate expertise, giving selected entrepreneurs an opportunity to learn from professionals and organisations with relevant experience.

This type of support can provide practical perspectives on issues such as

  • Business development
  • Scaling
  • Strategy
  • Operations
  • Innovation
  • Healthcare delivery
  • Partnerships
  • Impact development

4. Professional Networks

Entrepreneurs will also gain access to networks that can help them build relationships and potentially identify new opportunities for collaboration, partnerships and growth.

For a social enterprise seeking to scale its impact, access to relevant networks can be valuable for connecting with potential partners, experts and other stakeholders.

5. Peer-to-Peer Learning

Another important element of the programme is peer-to-peer learning.

Selected entrepreneurs will have the opportunity to interact with other social entrepreneurs working to solve significant social challenges.

This can create opportunities to exchange experiences, learn from different business models and understand how other entrepreneurs approach challenges related to growth and impact.

What Does the Programme Aim to Help Entrepreneurs Achieve?

The support offered through Entrepreneurs for Resilience is designed to help participating enterprises strengthen both their business models and social impact models.

The ultimate objective is to enable enterprises to:

  1. Strengthen their business and impact models.
  2. Expand the reach of their solutions.
  3. Reach more underserved communities.
  4. Improve access to affordable healthcare.
  5. Bring quality primary healthcare closer to communities.
  6. Develop sustainable approaches to healthcare delivery.
  7. Use digital and physical solutions to overcome healthcare access barriers.

The programme therefore goes beyond simply providing funding. It combines financial support with expertise, networks and learning opportunities intended to help social enterprises grow sustainably.

Who Is Behind Entrepreneurs for Resilience 2027?

The Swiss Re Foundation is leading the 2027 Entrepreneurs for Resilience programme.

For this edition, the Swiss Re Foundation is partnering with several organisations working in areas related to healthcare, inclusion and social impact.

The partners mentioned in the programme announcement include

  • Digital Connected Care Coalition (DCCC)
  • AXA EssentiALL
  • Sanofi’s Global Health Unit’s Impact Fund
  • Philips Foundation

These collaborations bring together organisations with expertise and networks that can support social enterprises working to expand healthcare access.

The partnership with the Digital Connected Care Coalition is particularly relevant given the programme’s emphasis on integrated digital and physical healthcare solutions.

Why Healthcare Access Is Central to the 2027 Programme

Healthcare access remains a major development challenge, particularly for populations that experience financial, geographical or infrastructural barriers.

A healthcare system may exist within a country, but this does not necessarily mean that every community can access appropriate services.

People living in underserved areas may face challenges such as travelling long distances to reach healthcare facilities, paying costs they cannot afford or encountering limited availability of quality services.

Digital technology has created new possibilities for addressing some of these challenges.

Telemedicine, digital health platforms and other technology-enabled services can help connect people with healthcare professionals and services. However, digital solutions alone may not address every healthcare need.

This is where the brick-and-click approach becomes relevant.

By combining physical healthcare infrastructure and services with digital technologies, social enterprises can develop more integrated approaches to healthcare delivery.

Entrepreneurs for Resilience 2027 is therefore looking for enterprises that are already working at the intersection of healthcare, technology, social entrepreneurship and community impact.

What Kind of Social Enterprises Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity may be particularly relevant to social enterprises that already have a healthcare solution and are looking to scale.

Potentially relevant enterprises could include organisations working on:

  • Affordable primary healthcare delivery
  • Community healthcare
  • Digital health
  • Telemedicine
  • Healthcare technology
  • Healthcare access platforms
  • Remote healthcare services
  • Technology-enabled clinics
  • Affordable diagnostic services
  • Digital patient services
  • Healthcare services for underserved populations
  • Integrated physical and digital healthcare models

The central consideration is whether the enterprise is helping expand affordable, quality primary healthcare for underserved populations in LMICs.

Entrepreneurs for Resilience 2027 Application Deadline

Applications for the 2027 edition of Entrepreneurs for Resilience are open from 7 September 2026 through 4 October 2026.

Deadline: 4 October 2026 at 23:59 CET

Applicants should pay close attention to the deadline and time zone when preparing their submissions.

The programme also states that only applications submitted in English before the deadline will be considered.

Entrepreneurs should therefore ensure that their applications are completed and submitted in English before the specified closing time.

How to Apply for Entrepreneurs for Resilience 2027

Interested entrepreneurs should first review the programme’s eligibility criteria and application requirements carefully.

The application process involves submitting an application through the official Entrepreneurs for Resilience application platform.

Applicants should ensure that they:

  1. Review the eligibility requirements.
  2. Confirm that their social enterprise aligns with the healthcare focus of the 2027 edition.
  3. Assess whether their solution addresses healthcare access challenges affecting underserved populations.
  4. Demonstrate how their model combines physical and/or digital approaches where relevant.
  5. Explain their existing impact and potential for further scale.
  6. Prepare the required application information in English.
  7. Submit the completed application before the deadline.

The official programme materials should be consulted for the complete eligibility criteria and application requirements before submitting an application.

APPLY HERE

What Applicants Should Highlight in Their Application

Although applicants should follow the official application requirements, social enterprises can use the application process to clearly communicate the key elements of their work.

A strong application should clearly explain the problem, the solution, the business model, the impact achieved so far and the potential for scale.

Important areas to communicate include:

The Healthcare Problem

Explain the specific healthcare access challenge the enterprise is addressing.

For example, applicants may describe how cost, distance, availability or other barriers affect the communities they serve.

The Solution

Clearly explain how the enterprise addresses the identified problem.

If the solution combines physical and digital healthcare services, applicants should explain how the two components work together.

The Target Population

Applicants should clearly identify the underserved populations benefiting from the solution.

This could include communities that face geographical, economic or other barriers to accessing quality healthcare.

Existing Impact

Where applicable, applicants should demonstrate measurable results.

Examples could include:

  • Number of people reached
  • Number of healthcare consultations delivered
  • Number of communities served
  • Reduction in healthcare access costs
  • Number of patients using digital services
  • Geographic expansion
  • Improvements in service accessibility

Scalability

Since the programme is focused on scaling impact, applicants should explain how their enterprise can expand its reach.

They should consider questions such as

  • Can the model be replicated in other communities?
  • What infrastructure is required for expansion?
  • What partnerships are needed?
  • How can technology support growth?
  • What additional resources are required?
  • How will the enterprise maintain quality as it scales?

Sustainability

Applicants should also demonstrate how the enterprise can maintain its operations and impact over time.

This is particularly important for social enterprises seeking to balance financial sustainability with social impact.

Benefits of Entrepreneurs for Resilience 2027

Participation in the programme can provide selected entrepreneurs with several forms of support.

These include:

  • Funding to support enterprise development and scaling.
  • Tailored advisory support to strengthen business and impact models.
  • Corporate expertise from experienced organisations and professionals.
  • Professional networks that can create opportunities for collaboration and growth.
  • Peer-to-peer learning with other social entrepreneurs.
  • Support for scaling impact and reaching additional underserved populations.
  • Opportunities to strengthen healthcare delivery models.
  • Exposure to a network of organisations working on resilience, healthcare and social impact.

Together, these resources can help social enterprises move toward greater scale while maintaining a focus on measurable social impact.

Why Social Entrepreneurs May Find This Opportunity Relevant

Social enterprises often face a unique challenge: they must develop financially sustainable operations while simultaneously addressing complex social problems.

Healthcare-focused enterprises can face additional challenges because delivering quality healthcare requires appropriate infrastructure, skilled professionals, technology and sustainable financing.

Entrepreneurs for Resilience provides a combination of resources designed to help selected enterprises navigate these challenges.

The programme’s 2027 focus is particularly relevant for entrepreneurs developing models that can make primary healthcare more affordable, accessible and available to underserved populations.

For enterprises that already have a functioning solution and are looking to expand, access to funding, expertise, networks and peer learning can support the next stage of development.

Key Details at a Glance

Organiser Swiss Re Foundation
Edition 10th edition
Focus Affordable, quality primary healthcare
Target communities Underserved populations in LMICs
Preferred model Brick-and-click healthcare models
Support Funding, advisory support, corporate expertise, networks and peer learning
Application language English
Applications open 7 September 2026
Application deadline 4 October 2026, 23:59 CET

Geographic focus Low- and middle-income countries
Application platform Swiss Re Foundation application portal

How Entrepreneurs for Resilience Can Contribute to Healthcare Innovation

The growing use of digital technologies in healthcare has created opportunities to rethink how primary healthcare is delivered.

However, technology is most useful when it responds to real community needs.

A digital platform, for example, may improve access to consultations, but some patients may still require physical examinations, diagnostic services, medicines or other forms of in-person care.

The brick-and-click model seeks to bring these different components together.

This approach can potentially create healthcare systems that are more connected to the communities they serve while using technology to improve efficiency, convenience and reach.

For social entrepreneurs, this creates opportunities to develop models that address healthcare challenges from multiple angles rather than relying on a single intervention.

Visit HERE for more information about the Entrepreneurs for Resilience 2027.

Conclusion

The Entrepreneurs for Resilience 2027 programme presents an opportunity for social enterprises working to improve access to affordable and quality primary healthcare for underserved populations in low- and middle-income countries.

Marking the 10th edition of the programme, the 2027 initiative places particular emphasis on brick-and-click healthcare models that combine physical and digital solutions to bring healthcare services closer to communities.

Selected entrepreneurs can receive funding, tailored advisory support, corporate expertise, professional networks and peer-to-peer learning, with the broader objective of strengthening their business and impact models and helping them reach more people.

Social enterprises developing scalable healthcare solutions should review the full eligibility requirements and application materials carefully and submit their applications in English before the 4 October 2026, 23:59 CET deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Embassy in Austria has announced a range of internship opportunities for students and emerging professionals interested in gaining practical experience in diplomacy, international affairs, public diplomacy, political and economic affairs, commercial diplomacy, multilateral affairs, public affairs, and international organizations.

Based in Vienna, Austria, these internships provide opportunities to gain exposure to the work of the U.S. Embassy in Austria, the U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Vienna (UNVIE), and the U.S. Mission to the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (USOSCE).

The internship opportunities are offered across several sections and have different recruitment and review schedules. Some sections are currently accepting applications for placements beginning in 2026, while others have upcoming review cycles in October 2026 or Spring 2027.

Applicants interested in international relations, diplomacy, communications, public affairs, political science, economics, international development, multilateral cooperation, trade, business, and related fields may find these opportunities particularly relevant.

Overview of the U.S. Embassy in Austria Internship Opportunities

The internship announcements cover three major U.S. diplomatic missions in Vienna:

  1. U.S. Embassy in Austria
  2. U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Vienna (UNVIE)
  3. U.S. Mission to the OSCE in Vienna (USOSCE)

Each mission includes different sections that offer internships according to their operational needs and recruitment schedules.

Because these are separate internship opportunities, applicants should not assume that the eligibility criteria, placement dates, application deadlines, or required qualifications are identical across all sections.

1. Internships at the U.S. Embassy in Austria

The U.S. Embassy in Austria has several sections that offer internship opportunities.

Public Diplomacy Section Internship

The Public Diplomacy Section offers an opportunity for individuals interested in communications, public engagement, international outreach, cultural diplomacy and related areas.

According to the announcement, the next review cycle is scheduled for October 2026.

Applications submitted before that review cycle will be considered for 2027 placements. However, the Embassy notes that applicants may be contacted earlier if additional internship opportunities become available.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to candidates interested in areas such as:

  • Public diplomacy
  • Strategic communications
  • International communications
  • Media and public affairs
  • Cultural exchange
  • Digital communications
  • Outreach and public engagement
  • International relations

Applicants with academic or professional backgrounds in communications, international relations, political science, diplomacy, media, public affairs or related fields may wish to examine the detailed section-specific requirements.

Commercial Service Internship

The U.S. Commercial Service at the U.S. Embassy in Vienna is also accepting applications.

The announcement states that applications are being accepted for Winter 2026 and onward.

This internship may be particularly relevant for candidates interested in the intersection of diplomacy and international business.

Potential areas of relevance include:

  • International trade
  • Business development
  • Commercial diplomacy
  • Market research
  • Economic relations
  • Export promotion
  • International business
  • Trade policy
  • Economic analysis

Candidates interested in international business, economics, commerce, finance, international relations or related fields should review the individual Commercial Service announcement for its specific requirements.

Political/Economic Section Internship

The Political/Economic Section provides another opportunity for candidates interested in diplomacy and international affairs.

The next review cycle is scheduled for October 2026, and applications submitted during the current period will be considered for placements beginning in Winter 2026.

The Political/Economic Section can be particularly relevant for applicants interested in:

  • Political affairs
  • International relations
  • Foreign policy
  • Economic affairs
  • Political analysis
  • Diplomatic reporting
  • European affairs
  • International security
  • Government relations

For students and graduates pursuing careers in diplomacy, foreign affairs, political analysis or international organizations, an internship in a political/economic environment can provide valuable exposure to professional diplomatic work.

Facilities Management Office Internship

The Facilities Management Office is listed among the U.S. Embassy’s internship opportunities. However, the announcement currently states that there is no vacancy.

Applicants interested in this area are advised to check the Embassy’s internship page for future announcements and recruitment timelines.

2. Internships at the U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Vienna

The U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Vienna, commonly referred to as UNVIE, represents another major source of internship opportunities.

Vienna is an important international diplomatic hub and hosts numerous international organizations. An internship within the U.S. Mission to International Organizations can therefore provide exposure to multilateral diplomacy and international institutional affairs.

The announcement identifies several sections.

Public Affairs Section Internship

The Public Affairs Section of the U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Vienna offers an internship opportunity for individuals interested in public affairs, communications and international outreach.

The next review cycle is scheduled for October 2026.

Applications submitted now will be considered for 2027 placements, while applicants may potentially be contacted earlier if additional opportunities arise.

This area may be particularly relevant for candidates with interests or experience in:

  • Public affairs
  • Strategic communications
  • Media relations
  • International communications
  • Digital media
  • Public diplomacy
  • Content development
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • International organizations

Candidates pursuing communications careers within governments, international organizations, diplomatic missions or development institutions may find this type of experience particularly relevant.

UN Affairs Office Internship

The UN Affairs Office also has an internship opportunity at the U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Vienna.

The next review cycle is October 2026, with applications submitted now being considered for 2027 placements.

The office may also contact applicants earlier if additional opportunities arise.

This internship is particularly relevant to individuals interested in:

  • United Nations affairs
  • Multilateral diplomacy
  • International organizations
  • International cooperation
  • Foreign policy
  • Global governance
  • Diplomatic relations
  • International negotiations
  • Multilateral policy

Applicants with backgrounds in international relations, political science, diplomacy, international security, development studies, law or related disciplines may wish to examine the detailed eligibility requirements.

Multilateral and Technical Affairs Section Internship

A new internship opportunity is also available within the Multilateral and Technical Affairs Section (MTA).

The announcement states that this section is accepting applications for Fall/Winter 2026 and onward.

This is particularly significant for applicants seeking experience in multilateral and technical policy environments.

The opportunity may appeal to candidates interested in areas involving:

  • Multilateral affairs
  • Technical diplomacy
  • International policy
  • International organizations
  • Global governance
  • Policy analysis
  • Diplomatic engagement
  • International cooperation

Applicants should consult the dedicated MTA internship announcement to determine the precise qualifications, eligibility requirements and application procedures.

3. Internships at the U.S. Mission to the OSCE in Vienna

The third group of opportunities is offered through the U.S. Mission to the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (USOSCE).

The OSCE is an important international organization working across areas including security, political cooperation and regional affairs.

Political Section Internship

The Political Section of the U.S. Mission to the OSCE has an upcoming review cycle scheduled for Spring 2027.

Candidates interested in political affairs, international security, diplomacy and European regional affairs may find this opportunity relevant.

Potential areas of interest include:

  • International security
  • Political affairs
  • Foreign policy
  • European affairs
  • Diplomacy
  • Conflict prevention
  • International cooperation
  • Regional security

Applicants should check the dedicated announcement when applying because the recruitment timeline and eligibility requirements may differ from the other internships listed by the U.S. Embassy in Austria.

Public Diplomacy Section Internship

The Public Diplomacy Section at the U.S. Mission to the OSCE is also accepting applications for Fall/Winter 2026 and onward.

This provides an opportunity for applicants interested in communications, public diplomacy and international engagement.

Relevant academic and professional interests may include:

  • Communications
  • Public diplomacy
  • Media
  • International relations
  • Public affairs
  • Digital communications
  • Strategic communications
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • International organizations

Internship Opportunities and Review Timelines

The opportunities currently listed by the U.S. Mission in Austria have different recruitment schedules.

Section Current Status Review/Placement Timeline
U.S. Embassy Public Diplomacy Accepting applications Next review cycle: October 2026; applications considered for 2027 placements
U.S. Embassy Commercial Service Accepting applications Winter 2026 and onward
U.S. Embassy Political/Economic Accepting applications Next review cycle: October 2026; placements starting Winter 2026
Facilities Management Office No current vacancy Check back for future opportunities
UNVIE Public Affairs Accepting applications Next review cycle: October 2026; applications considered for 2027
UNVIE UN Affairs Office Accepting applications Next review cycle: October 2026; applications considered for 2027
UNVIE Multilateral and Technical Affairs Accepting applications Fall/Winter 2026 and onward
USOSCE Political Section Upcoming Next review cycle: Spring 2027
USOSCE Public Diplomacy Accepting applications Fall/Winter 2026 and onward

Important: These are section-specific recruitment cycles rather than one universal deadline. Applicants should therefore pay close attention to the specific internship announcement for the section they wish to join.

What Makes These Internships Relevant for International Affairs Careers?

An internship within a diplomatic mission can provide exposure to professional environments where international relations, government affairs, communications and policy intersect.

Depending on the section, interns may gain exposure to areas such as:

1. Diplomatic Affairs

Political and multilateral sections can expose interns to the practical workings of diplomacy and international engagement.

2. International Organizations

The Vienna location is particularly significant because it is home to a range of international institutions. Internships connected to UNVIE can therefore provide insight into multilateral engagement.

3. Strategic Communications

Public Diplomacy and Public Affairs internships can be relevant to individuals seeking careers in strategic communications, media, public engagement and international outreach.

4. Political and Economic Analysis

The Political/Economic Section can be relevant to applicants interested in political developments, economic affairs and foreign policy.

5. International Trade and Business

The Commercial Service opportunity provides exposure to the relationship between diplomacy and international commerce.

6. Multilateral Policy

The Multilateral and Technical Affairs internship can provide experience in a policy environment involving international cooperation and technical affairs.

7. International Security

The USOSCE Political Section may be particularly relevant to candidates interested in international security, regional diplomacy and political affairs.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunities may be particularly relevant to:

  • University students seeking practical international experience.
  • Recent graduates interested in diplomacy and foreign affairs.
  • Students studying international relations.
  • Political science students.
  • Diplomacy and international security students.
  • Communications and public relations students.
  • Journalism and media students.
  • Economics and international business students.
  • International development students.
  • Public policy students.
  • International law students.
  • Candidates interested in multilateral organizations.
  • Individuals pursuing careers in diplomatic missions.
  • Candidates interested in public diplomacy and public affairs.
  • Students seeking experience related to the United Nations or OSCE.

However, eligibility is not uniform across all sections. Applicants should verify the requirements stated in the individual internship announcement before submitting an application.

Countries and Nationality Eligibility

The announcement provided does not state one universal nationality requirement covering all of the internships.

This is an important distinction because internships associated with a U.S. diplomatic mission can have section-specific eligibility requirements, including requirements relating to citizenship, residency, student status or other conditions.

Therefore, applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania or other regions should not assume eligibility solely on the basis of geographic location.

The appropriate approach is to open the specific internship announcement and confirm:

  1. Who is eligible to apply.
  2. Whether U.S. citizenship is required.
  3. Whether Austrian citizenship or residency is required.
  4. Whether applicants from other nationalities are eligible.
  5. Whether the applicant must currently be enrolled at a university.
  6. Whether recent graduates are eligible.
  7. Whether there are age or other eligibility requirements.
  8. Whether the applicant must be legally resident in Austria.
  9. Whether there are language requirements.
  10. Whether additional documentation is required.

This is especially important for international applicants considering the opportunities from outside Austria.

Application Deadlines and Review Dates

There is no single deadline for all of the internships.

Instead, the opportunities operate according to individual recruitment schedules.

Key dates listed in the announcement include:

  • October 2026: Next review cycle for the U.S. Embassy Public Diplomacy Section.
  • October 2026: Next review cycle for the U.S. Embassy Political/Economic Section.
  • October 2026: Next review cycle for the UNVIE Public Affairs Section.
  • October 2026: Next review cycle for the UNVIE UN Affairs Office.
  • Fall/Winter 2026 onward: Applications accepted for the UNVIE Multilateral and Technical Affairs Section.
  • Fall/Winter 2026 onward: Applications accepted for the USOSCE Public Diplomacy Section.
  • Winter 2026 onward: Applications accepted for the U.S. Embassy Commercial Service.
  • Spring 2027: Next review cycle for the USOSCE Political Section.

Applicants should note that the October 2026 review cycle is particularly important, because several of the listed internships use October as their next review point.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should begin by identifying the section that most closely matches their academic background and career interests.

The U.S. Embassy in Austria provides individual announcements for each internship rather than treating all placements as one application.

Applicants should therefore:

  1. Choose the appropriate internship section.
  2. Read the complete section-specific announcement.
  3. Check nationality and eligibility requirements.
  4. Confirm the expected placement period.
  5. Review the required application documents.
  6. Prepare an updated CV or résumé.
  7. Prepare any required motivation statement or cover letter.
  8. Ensure that academic information is accurate and up-to-date.
  9. Submit the application through the designated application process.
  10. Monitor the relevant announcement for future review cycles or additional opportunities.

Applicants should avoid submitting a generic application without first checking the requirements for their preferred section.

APPLY HERE

Tips for Preparing a Strong Internship Application

Although the requirements differ between sections, applicants can strengthen their applications by clearly connecting their background to the work of the particular office.

Demonstrate relevant academic preparation.

Highlight coursework or academic projects relevant to the internship.

For example:

  • International relations
  • Diplomacy
  • Political science
  • Economics
  • International security
  • Communications
  • Journalism
  • International development
  • Public policy
  • International law
  • Business or trade

Highlight practical experience.

Applicants should clearly demonstrate relevant experience from:

  • Previous internships
  • Research projects
  • University organizations
  • Volunteer work
  • Communications projects
  • Policy research
  • International conferences
  • Student leadership
  • Community engagement
  • Journalism or media work

Tailor the application to the section.

A candidate applying to Public Diplomacy should emphasize communications, public engagement and media skills, while someone applying to a Political/Economic Section should demonstrate relevant analytical and international affairs experience.

Similarly, an applicant interested in the Commercial Service should highlight relevant business, economics, trade or market-related experience.

Demonstrate international awareness.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate an understanding of international affairs and an interest in working in a multicultural environment.

Pay attention to application timing.

Because the opportunities have different review cycles, applicants should not wait until the final moment to prepare their documents.

For sections with October 2026 review cycles, applicants should ensure their applications are ready before the relevant review process begins.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this one internship programme?

No. The announcement brings together multiple internship opportunities across different U.S. diplomatic missions and sections in Vienna.

Are all the internships currently accepting applications?

No. Some are accepting applications, while others have upcoming review cycles, and the Facilities Management Office currently has no vacancy.

Are these internships paid?

The material provided does not establish a universal stipend or salary for all of the internships. Applicants should consult the individual internship announcement for information concerning compensation, expenses and other placement conditions.

Can international students apply?

Eligibility depends on the specific internship. The general announcement does not establish a single nationality rule applicable to every opportunity. International applicants should check the individual section’s requirements.

Can applicants from Africa apply?

Applicants from Africa should not assume either eligibility or ineligibility based solely on their continent. The relevant section’s individual announcement should be checked for nationality, residency and other requirements.

Are recent graduates eligible?

This depends on the individual internship. Applicants should verify whether the specific section requires current student status or accepts recent graduates.

When is the next major review cycle?

Introduction

The Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance offers an opportunity for students seeking advanced specialisation and research training in economics, finance, law and business. The programme is designed for individuals who wish to pursue academic or professional careers in institutions where advanced economic, financial, business or statistical knowledge is required.

Through its research-focused approach, the programme aims to advance knowledge in economics, business and the social sciences while contributing to the analysis of important economic problems. It provides students with the tools needed to conduct advanced research, examine complex economic issues and formulate economic alternatives and policies that can contribute to economic development.

The programme brings together four main research areas: Economics, Finance, Business and Law. These areas provide a broad foundation for investigating economic and financial challenges, developing new knowledge and exploring solutions to issues affecting businesses, institutions and society.

In addition to its academic and research objectives, the Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance offers an international learning environment, experienced faculty, opportunities for research collaboration and an intellectually stimulating atmosphere that encourages critical thinking and cooperation.

About the Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance

The Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance is intended for students who want to develop advanced expertise in areas related to economics, finance, law and business. Its objective is to prepare individuals for careers that require a strong understanding of economic and financial systems, analytical methods, statistical techniques and research.

The programme is particularly relevant to people interested in working in academic institutions, central banks, research departments, public-sector organisations, private-sector entities and other institutions that rely on advanced economic, financial or statistical skills.

A central objective of the programme is to contribute to the advancement of knowledge. Through doctoral-level research, students can investigate important economic and social questions, develop new insights and contribute to discussions about economic development and policy.

The programme also seeks to equip researchers with the tools required to conduct research at the frontier of knowledge. This emphasis on advanced research enables students to explore existing economic challenges, examine alternative approaches and contribute evidence that may inform economic decisions and policies.

Objectives of the Doctoral Programme

The programme has several interconnected objectives that guide its academic and research activities.

1. Provide Advanced Specialisation

The programme offers advanced specialisation in Economics, Finance, Law and Business. This allows students to develop deeper knowledge in their chosen research area and acquire expertise relevant to academic research or professional work.

Advanced specialisation is particularly important in institutions where economic decisions, financial analysis, statistical research and policy development require a high level of technical knowledge.

2. Prepare Students for Academic and Professional Careers

The programme is designed for individuals who intend to pursue academic or professional careers.

For those interested in academia, doctoral research provides an opportunity to develop research skills and contribute to the advancement of knowledge in their chosen field. For those pursuing professional careers, the programme aims to develop advanced analytical and research capabilities that can be applied in institutions such as central banks, public and private research departments, and other organisations.

3. Advance Economic, Business and Social Knowledge

Another important objective is to advance the frontier of knowledge in economics, business and the social sciences.

The programme encourages research that contributes to a deeper understanding of economic and social issues. By investigating relevant problems and developing new findings, doctoral researchers can help expand the knowledge available to academics, policymakers, businesses and other institutions.

4. Analyse Important Economic Problems

The programme seeks to contribute to the analysis of the most relevant economic problems.

Economic challenges often involve complex relationships between markets, institutions, financial systems, businesses and society. Doctoral research can help investigate these relationships, identify underlying issues and develop a more detailed understanding of the problems being examined.

5. Develop Research-Based Economic Alternatives and Policies

The programme provides the tools needed to carry out advanced research that can support the formulation of economic alternatives and policies geared towards economic development.

This objective connects academic research with practical economic questions. Through research, students can examine different approaches to economic challenges and contribute knowledge that may help inform policy discussions and development strategies.

The Four Research Areas

The Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance is organised around four research lines: Economics, Finance, Business and Law. These areas provide the programme’s central fields of academic specialisation.

1. Economics

The Economics research line provides a foundation for investigating economic issues and contributing to the understanding of how economies function.

Research in economics can be relevant to questions involving economic development, public policy, markets, institutions and broader economic challenges. The programme’s stated objective of analysing important economic problems makes this research area particularly relevant to students interested in producing knowledge that can inform economic alternatives and policies.

Economics research can also support careers in academic institutions, central banks, research departments and other organisations that require advanced economic expertise.

2. Finance

The Finance research line is relevant to students interested in advanced financial analysis and research.

Financial knowledge is important in institutions that examine financial systems, evaluate economic and financial conditions, and make decisions that require specialised analytical skills. The programme’s emphasis on advanced financial and statistical capabilities makes this research line relevant to individuals seeking careers in financial institutions, central banks, research departments and other organisations.

Through doctoral research, students can pursue specialised questions within finance and contribute to the development of knowledge in the field.

3. Business

The Business research line provides an opportunity to investigate issues related to businesses and their economic and social environments.

Business research can contribute to a better understanding of organisational and economic challenges and support the development of knowledge relevant to professional and academic settings.

The programme’s broader objective of advancing business and social knowledge means that this research line forms part of its contribution to understanding important issues affecting institutions and the economy.

4. Law

The Law research line provides a further area of specialisation within the doctoral programme.

Its inclusion reflects the programme’s broad approach to advanced study across economics, finance, law and business. It offers a research pathway for students whose academic interests involve legal questions connected to the programme’s wider fields of study.

Together, the four research lines create a broad academic structure through which doctoral students can pursue specialised research and contribute to knowledge in their chosen area.

Faculty with International Research Experience and Recognition

One of the programme’s stated features is its faculty, which has international research experience and recognition.

An experienced research faculty can contribute to an academic environment in which students engage with advanced ideas, develop research questions and strengthen their understanding of their chosen fields.

The programme’s emphasis on international research experience also reflects its commitment to connecting doctoral study with wider academic research. This is relevant to students who want to undertake advanced research and develop expertise that can be applied in academic or professional institutions.

The programme identifies its faculty as an important part of the learning and research environment it offers.

An International Academic Environment

The Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance offers an international environment that enables it to attract students from different countries.

An international academic environment can bring together individuals with different educational experiences, perspectives and research interests. This can create opportunities for academic exchange and discussion across different economic, financial, business and legal contexts.

The programme’s international orientation is also reflected in its emphasis on research exchanges with leading universities and research institutions.

For students interested in developing an international academic or professional outlook, this environment forms an important part of the programme’s overall offering.

However, the programme information provided does not specify particular eligible countries, nationality requirements or geographical restrictions. Prospective applicants should contact the programme directly if they require confirmation of country-specific eligibility.

Research Opportunities at the Frontier of Knowledge

The programme offers what it describes as an attractive set of research lines linked to the frontier of knowledge in different areas.

Research at the frontier of knowledge involves engaging with current questions and developing work that can contribute to the advancement of a field. Within this programme, the four research lines provide the broad areas in which students can pursue specialised academic research.

The programme’s research orientation is closely connected to its objective of advancing economic, business and social knowledge. Rather than focusing only on the acquisition of existing knowledge, it aims to provide the tools needed for students to conduct research and contribute new insights.

This focus is particularly relevant for individuals who want to develop advanced research capabilities for academic careers or professional roles that involve complex analysis.

An Intellectually Active and Stimulating Research Environment

The programme places emphasis on creating an intellectually active and stimulating atmosphere.

Its academic environment is designed to encourage critical thinking, cooperation and joint research. These elements are important in doctoral study, where students are expected to engage deeply with research questions, assess ideas critically and contribute to the development of knowledge.

The programme also fosters international research exchanges with leading universities and research institutions, alongside cooperative research programmes.

These activities reflect an approach to doctoral education that values collaboration and engagement with the wider research community.

Critical Thinking

Critical thinking is an important part of advanced research. Researchers must be able to examine questions carefully, assess evidence, consider different explanations and develop reasoned conclusions.

The programme’s emphasis on critical thinking supports its objective of preparing students to analyse relevant economic problems and contribute to the advancement of knowledge.

Cooperation and Joint Research

The programme also emphasises cooperation and joint research.

Research collaboration allows scholars to exchange ideas, work together on questions of shared interest and draw on different areas of expertise. The programme’s focus on cooperation is consistent with its wider aim of creating an active academic environment.

International Research Exchanges

International research exchanges provide opportunities for engagement with leading universities and research institutions.

The programme identifies these exchanges, together with cooperative research programmes, as part of the academic environment it seeks to foster. These connections can support the exchange of research ideas and contribute to a broader understanding of developments in economics, finance, business and law.

APPLY HERE

Who Should Consider the Doctoral Programme?

The programme is intended for students who wish to pursue advanced specialisation and research in Economics, Finance, Law or Business.

It may be particularly relevant to individuals who are interested in:

  • Pursuing an academic career involving teaching or research.
  • Developing advanced expertise in economics, finance, business or law.
  • Working in central banks or economic and financial institutions.
  • Joining research departments in public or private organisations.
  • Conducting research on important economic and social problems.
  • Contributing to the development of economic alternatives and policies.
  • Building advanced analytical, financial, economic or statistical skills.

The programme’s stated purpose is to prepare students for academic and professional careers that require advanced skills. The information provided does not specify the precise academic qualifications, grades, language requirements, professional experience or other admission criteria. Applicants should request the official admission requirements directly from the programme.

Career Relevance and Potential Professional Pathways

The Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance is designed to develop expertise relevant to institutions that require advanced economic, financial or statistical skills.

The programme specifically identifies several types of institutions in which such expertise may be useful.

Academic Institutions

Students interested in academic careers can use doctoral research to develop specialised knowledge and research capabilities. The programme’s emphasis on advancing knowledge, critical thinking and joint research is relevant to individuals who intend to contribute to academic research.

Central Banks

Central banks are among the institutions identified in the programme description as requiring advanced skills in economic, financial or statistical fields.

The programme’s research areas and focus on economic problem analysis are relevant to individuals interested in developing expertise for work in such institutions.

Public and Private Research Departments

The programme also identifies research departments in public and private entities as potential professional settings.

These organisations may require people who can conduct advanced research, analyse complex issues and contribute to evidence-based work. The programme’s emphasis on research methods and the development of economic knowledge is aligned with these broad professional needs.

Other Organisations Requiring Advanced Expertise

The programme is also intended for students who wish to work in other organisations that require advanced economic, financial or statistical skills.

The range of research lines means that the programme is not limited to one professional sector. Its relevance will depend on the student’s research specialisation and the requirements of the institution or career they intend to pursue.

These are potential career pathways identified by the programme’s stated objectives, not guarantees of employment after graduation.

How to Obtain Further Information

Individuals who would like to learn more about the Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance can contact the programme directly by email.

Email: doctoralprogrammes@cunef.edu

Prospective applicants can use this contact to request further information about the programme, including its admission requirements, application process, research opportunities and other details not included in the general programme description.

Before making an application, interested students should seek confirmation of the academic qualifications required, the application timeline, any applicable fees or funding arrangements, and the documents that must be submitted.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance

Application Deadline and Funding Information

The programme information provided does not state an application deadline.

It also does not specify whether the doctoral programme offers scholarships, tuition waivers, stipends or other financial support. Prospective applicants should contact the programme directly to confirm the current application period, fees and any available funding opportunities.

Conclusion

The Doctoral Programme in Economics and Finance offers advanced specialisation and research opportunities across Economics, Finance, Business and Law. It is designed for students who wish to pursue academic or professional careers in institutions that require advanced economic, financial or statistical expertise.

Its central objectives include advancing economic, business and social knowledge, analysing important economic problems, and providing the tools needed to conduct research that can contribute to economic alternatives and development-oriented policies.

The programme’s international research faculty, international academic environment, research lines and emphasis on critical thinking, cooperation and joint research form the foundation of its academic offering. It also seeks to foster research exchanges with leading universities and research institutions and to encourage cooperative research programmes.

For individuals interested in doctoral-level research and careers in academia, central banking, public or private research departments, and other institutions requiring advanced expertise, the programme may be worth exploring.

Those interested in pursuing this opportunity should contact doctoralprogrammes@cunef.edu for further details about admission requirements, application procedures, deadlines, fees and potential funding opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The 2027–2028 APAICS Congressional Fellowship offers an opportunity for individuals interested in public policy, government, legislation, and civic engagement to gain practical experience within the United States Congress. The fellowship places participants in a congressional office or committee for 12 months, where they undertake work comparable to that of a congressional legislative aide.

The programme is designed to help fellows develop a deeper understanding of the legislative process, gain practical policy experience, build professional networks, and develop skills that can be applied to future careers in congressional offices, federal agencies, nonprofit organizations, and the private sector.

The fellowship will run from August 30, 2027, to August 25, 2028, and will take place in Washington, D.C. The application deadline is December 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET.

About the APAICS Congressional Fellowship

The APAICS Congressional Fellowship is structured around practical participation in the legislative process. Rather than being limited to classroom-based learning, fellows are placed directly within a congressional environment where they can gain experience working on matters related to public policy and legislative activities.

During the 12-month fellowship, participants will be placed with either a congressional office or a congressional committee. Their responsibilities will depend on the office or committee where they are placed and the specific policy portfolio assigned to them.

The programme states that fellows will undertake work equivalent to that of a congressional legislative aide. This provides fellows with an opportunity to develop practical knowledge of how Congress operates while contributing to the activities of their host office.

By completing the fellowship, participants are expected to develop a stronger understanding of the U.S. legislative process and establish professional relationships on Capitol Hill.

What Fellows Can Gain from the Programme

The fellowship is designed to provide participants with professional and policy-related development throughout the programme.

One major benefit is the opportunity to gain first-hand experience of the U.S. legislative process. Working within a congressional office or committee allows fellows to observe and participate in the processes through which public policy is discussed and developed.

Fellows can also develop professional skills that may be useful beyond the fellowship. According to the programme description, the experience can help fellows acquire skills and expertise that are marketable to congressional offices, federal agencies, nonprofit organizations, and private-sector employers.

The programme also provides an opportunity to develop a professional network on Capitol Hill. Because fellows work within congressional environments and participate in APAICS activities, they can interact with professionals involved in public policy and government.

Another important aspect is professional development. Fellows are required to meet as a cohort twice every month to discuss their experiences and participate in professional development opportunities. This provides a structured environment in which participants can reflect on their work, exchange experiences, and learn from other fellows.

Congressional Office or Committee Placement

Each fellow’s experience will be different because placements and responsibilities depend on the congressional office or committee to which they are assigned.

The policy portfolio given to a fellow will therefore determine much of the day-to-day experience. This means that participants may have different responsibilities depending on the policy issues and legislative work handled by their host office.

The programme provides fellows with the opportunity to work in a professional congressional environment while developing an understanding of how Congress functions.

This practical component is particularly relevant for individuals who are interested in careers involving public policy, government relations, legislative affairs, advocacy, public administration, international affairs, or related fields.

Fellowship Duration and Location

The 2027–2028 APAICS Congressional Fellowship will run for approximately 12 months.

The programme dates are:

Start date: August 30, 2027
End date: August 25, 2028
Location: Washington, D.C.

Washington, D.C. is the centre of the U.S. federal government and provides the setting for the fellowship’s congressional placement.

Participants should therefore be prepared for an extended period in Washington, D.C., rather than a short-term programme.

Fellows Are Not Federal Government Employees

An important distinction in the programme description is that APAICS Congressional Fellows are not employees of the federal government, their host congressional office, or APAICS.

Instead, fellows receive a monthly educational stipend during the fellowship.

This distinction is important for applicants to understand because the fellowship provides professional experience within a congressional environment without making the fellow a federal government employee.

Cohort Meetings and Professional Development

In addition to their work within their assigned congressional offices or committees, fellows are expected to participate in activities organized for the fellowship cohort.

Fellows are required to gather twice each month to discuss their experiences and participate in professional development opportunities.

These meetings provide an opportunity for participants to learn from one another and discuss the different experiences they encounter during their congressional placements.

The fellowship also expects participants to attend events organized by APAICS. These include the organization’s Annual Awards Gala and policy summits.

Public Policy Presentation

Another important requirement of the fellowship is a public presentation.

Towards the end of the fellowship year, fellows are required to make a public presentation on a policy topic of their choosing.

This requirement gives participants an opportunity to demonstrate their understanding of a policy issue and communicate their ideas publicly after gaining practical experience during the fellowship.

The presentation also complements the fellowship’s broader emphasis on professional development, policy knowledge, and communication.

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the 2027–2028 APAICS Congressional Fellowship is:

December 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM Eastern Time.

Applicants should ensure that their application materials are submitted before the stated deadline. The same deadline also applies to the submission of recommendation letters through the recommender portal.

The fellowship itself begins on August 30, 2027, and concludes on August 25, 2028.

How to Apply

Applicants are required to submit a complete application containing several components.

The application includes:

  1. Cover letter expressing interest in the programme.
  2. Resume, which must be no more than one page.
  3. Academic transcript.
  4. Two letters of recommendation.
  5. Responses to three application questions.

The recommendation letters can be submitted separately by the recommenders through the designated recommendation portal.

Applicants should also pay attention to the formatting requirements for the three written responses. Each response should be no more than one page, double-spaced, and written in 12-point Times New Roman font.

Application Question One

The first question asks applicants to explain how they envision the APAICS Fellowship contributing to their career path and what they hope to gain from the programme.

This question gives applicants an opportunity to explain their professional goals and connect those goals to the experience offered by the fellowship.

A strong response would therefore need to clearly explain the applicant’s career direction, why congressional and public policy experience is relevant to that direction, and what knowledge, skills, or professional experience they hope to develop.

Application Question Two

The second question focuses specifically on the applicant’s experience with Asian American, Native Hawaiian, or Pacific Islander communities in the United States.

Applicants are asked to describe when they have lived near or far from these communities and explain how that proximity, or lack of proximity, has shaped their views on public policy.

This question requires applicants to reflect on their personal experiences and connect those experiences to their understanding of public policy.

Visit HERE to learn more about the 2027–2028 APAICS Congressional Fellowship

Application Question Three

The third question focuses on teamwork and problem-solving.

Applicants are asked to describe a time when they worked as part of a team and encountered a challenge. They must discuss the challenges they experienced individually and as a team, explain how they contributed to addressing the challenge, and describe what they learned about working with others.

This question allows applicants to demonstrate their teamwork, communication, problem-solving, adaptability, and ability to learn from experience.

Recommendation Letters

Applicants are required to obtain two letters of recommendation.

The programme provides a separate online portal where recommenders can submit their letters.

The recommendation deadline is the same as the main application deadline:

December 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET.

Applicants should therefore allow sufficient time for their recommenders to complete and submit their letters before the deadline.

Why the Fellowship Can Be Relevant to Public Policy Careers

The structure of the APAICS Congressional Fellowship provides participants with exposure to several aspects of public policy work.

A fellow working within a congressional office or committee can gain an understanding of how legislative institutions operate while developing professional experience in a policy environment.

The combination of congressional placement, cohort meetings, professional development, APAICS events, networking opportunities, and a final public policy presentation makes the programme broader than a conventional short-term work placement.

The experience can be particularly relevant to people considering future careers involving public policy, legislative affairs, government, nonprofit organizations, federal agencies, advocacy, public administration, or related areas.

Important Information for Prospective Applicants

Before applying, prospective applicants should carefully review the official fellowship information, eligibility requirements, frequently asked questions, and host office information.

Fellowship Details and Eligibility

APAICS Fellowship Details and Eligibility

Host Office FAQs

Host Office FAQs

Conclusion

The 2027–2028 APAICS Congressional Fellowship provides a 12-month opportunity to gain practical experience within the U.S. congressional environment while developing knowledge of public policy and the legislative process. Fellows are placed in congressional offices or committees and undertake work comparable to that of congressional legislative aides, with each placement differing according to the host office and assigned policy portfolio.

In addition to their congressional placement, fellows participate in twice-monthly cohort meetings, professional development activities, APAICS events, and a public policy presentation at the end of the fellowship. The programme also provides a monthly educational stipend and opportunities to develop professional networks on Capitol Hill.

The fellowship will take place in Washington, D.C., from August 30, 2027, to August 25, 2028. Interested applicants should prepare the required cover letter, one-page resume, academic transcript, two recommendation letters, and responses to the three application questions before the December 18, 2026, 11:59 PM ET deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The American Institute for Boys and Men (AIBM) is inviting applications for its Graduate Research Fellowship, supporting emerging scholars conducting rigorous empirical research on issues affecting boys and men.

The fellowship provides $10,000 per year for up to two years and is designed to help build a stronger research field and cohort of scholars studying the challenges and opportunities facing boys and men. AIBM describes its work as focused on rigorous, objective and non-partisan research intended to improve the wellbeing of boys and men.

For the current fellowship cycle, AIBM is particularly interested in research examining men’s employment and labor force participation, online gambling, gaming and pornography, modern fatherhood, and social connection and civic engagement among young men.

About the AIBM Graduate Research Fellowship

The Graduate Research Fellowship is intended to support graduate researchers whose work aligns with AIBM’s mission.

The programme welcomes rigorous empirical research on topics related to boys and men, while maintaining particular areas of interest for the current application cycle.

AIBM’s fellowship programme is part of its broader effort to develop a community of researchers and scholars producing evidence on issues affecting boys and men.

Fellowship Award

Selected fellows receive:

$10,000 per year for up to two years.

Based on AIBM’s published fellowship information, fellowship funds can support research-related expenses such as:

  • Interviews
  • Fieldwork
  • Experiments
  • Research participants
  • Data purchases
  • Stipend support
  • Conferences
  • Travel
  • Fees
  • Contributions from project collaborators

The published fellowship guidelines state that the grants cannot cover indirect overhead.

Research Areas of Interest

AIBM states that applications can address any topic related to boys and men, provided the proposed work is rigorous and empirical.

For the current cycle, the organization has identified several areas of particular interest.

1. Men’s Employment and Labor Force Participation

AIBM is interested in research examining the causes and consequences of declining employment and labor force participation among men, particularly men without a four-year college degree.

Potential research may examine questions related to employment patterns, economic opportunity, workforce participation and the factors affecting men’s connection to the labor market.

2. Online Gambling, Gaming and Pornography

Another area of interest is understanding the effects of online gambling, gaming and pornography on boys and men.

This area aligns with AIBM’s broader Boys & Men Online initiative, which examines how digital technologies and online environments influence the social, emotional and financial lives of boys and men. The initiative currently studies areas including sports betting, pornography, gaming, AI companions and cryptocurrency/day-trading.

3. Modern Fatherhood

AIBM is also seeking research that can contribute to a modern, inclusive, strengths-based vision of fatherhood.

This aligns with AIBM’s broader Modern Fatherhood initiative, which examines fatherhood, father figures and the role of fathers and other male role models in the lives of boys and young men.

4. Social Connection, Belonging and Civic Engagement

The current fellowship call also highlights research that can build evidence for solutions strengthening:

  • Social connection
  • Belonging
  • Civic engagement

The particular focus is on young men and approaches that may strengthen their connections to communities and civic life.

Who Can Apply?

The current AIBM fellowship information indicates that the fellowship is intended for graduate students conducting research aligned with the Institute’s mission. AIBM’s published fellowship posting specifies that applicants must be currently enrolled in a Ph.D. programme at an accredited university in the United States.

The programme welcomes researchers from multiple academic disciplines, including:

  • Economics
  • Political science
  • Sociology
  • Psychology
  • Public policy
  • Education

Both qualitative and quantitative research are welcomed.

Students may be at the dissertation stage and seeking support, but applicants do not necessarily have to be at the dissertation stage.

What Kind of Research Is AIBM Looking For?

AIBM’s published fellowship information emphasizes research that is:

  • Rigorous
  • Empirical
  • Relevant to boys and men
  • Capable of contributing to the broader field
  • Potentially useful for policy discussions and interventions

The Institute’s fellowship programme seeks scholars whose research can contribute to understanding challenges and opportunities affecting boys and men and potentially inform policies and practices.

Applicants whose proposed topic does not fall neatly within one of the highlighted areas may still apply if they can demonstrate a strong connection to the broader field.

Building a Field of Study

AIBM’s fellowship programme is not only intended to fund individual research projects. The organization also describes the fellowship as part of an effort to build a robust field of study and cohort of scholars focused on boys and men.

AIBM currently maintains a community of staff, fellows and student fellows working across areas including education, employment, health, gambling, fatherhood and digital environments.

Examples of Research Areas Within AIBM’s Broader Work

AIBM’s existing fellows and student fellows work on a variety of research questions, including:

  • Boys’ education
  • Men’s employment
  • Family and fatherhood
  • Men’s health
  • Gambling
  • Online pornography
  • Male teachers
  • Social and emotional development
  • Economic policy
  • Civic outcomes
  • Digital behavior

This illustrates the breadth of research that can fall within the organization’s wider mission.

Application Deadline

The current application deadline is:

15 December 2026

The deadline has been confirmed in AIBM’s current fellowship announcement and related announcement from AIBM representatives.

Applicants should complete and submit their application before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day.

How to Apply

Interested graduate researchers should consult the American Institute for Boys and Men Careers and Opportunities page for the current Graduate Research Fellowship application information.

Applicants should carefully review the fellowship requirements and ensure that their research proposal clearly explains:

  1. The research question.
  2. The relevance of the research to boys and men.
  3. The empirical approach.
  4. The expected contribution to the field.
  5. How the research could contribute to policy or practical solutions where appropriate.

Tips for Preparing Your Application

Clearly Define the Research Question

A strong proposal should clearly explain the problem being investigated and why the question matters.

Demonstrate Rigorous Research

AIBM specifically emphasizes rigorous empirical research, so applicants should clearly explain their proposed methodology and evidence base.

Connect the Work to Boys and Men

Make the connection between the proposed research and the wellbeing, experiences, opportunities or challenges of boys and men clear.

Consider Policy Relevance

Research that can contribute to policy discussions or interventions is particularly relevant to the fellowship’s stated objectives.

Show How the Fellowship Supports the Project

Applicants should explain how the fellowship funding would help advance their research, whether through data acquisition, fieldwork, participant recruitment, travel, conferences or other eligible research expenses.

Conclusion

The AIBM Graduate Research Fellowship offers Ph.D. students an opportunity to receive $10,000 per year for up to two years while conducting research related to boys and men.

The current call welcomes rigorous empirical research across a broad range of topics, with particular interest in men’s employment and labor force participation, online gambling/gaming/pornography, modern fatherhood, and social connection, belonging and civic engagement among young men.

According to AIBM’s published fellowship information, eligible applicants are Ph.D. students enrolled at accredited U.S. universities, with applications welcomed from multiple disciplines and both qualitative and quantitative research traditions.
