item.content:encoded:
Schools and community partners in selected LyondellBasell communities in the United States can apply for the 2026–2027 Greening STEM Grant, an environmental education funding opportunity designed to support student-centered STEM projects focused on local environmental issues.

The initiative is offered through the Environmental Education Initiative (EEI) by Discovery Education, in partnership with the National Environmental Education Foundation (NEEF) and LyondellBasell (LYB).

During the 2026–2027 school year, the initiative will select two cohorts of five Greening STEM projects, with each selected project receiving a $5,000 grant.

The programme is designed to engage students in environmental science, encourage informed decision-making about healthy environments, and promote civic engagement through authentic STEM learning experiences.

About the Greening STEM Grant

The $5,000 grants will support holistic STEM programmes that incorporate environmental science and related resources into school curricula.

Projects should focus on student-directed investigations involving relevant research questions, local environmental issues, or challenges affecting local public lands.

Funding can help educators develop STEM programming that gives students opportunities to participate in place-based learning and environmental monitoring.

The initiative seeks to provide students with authentic STEM learning experiences in which the environment serves as a context for engagement and learning.

What the Grant Supports

The Greening STEM Grant supports projects that use STEM-focused content, instructional strategies, training approaches, collaboration and dissemination technologies to strengthen learning both inside and outside the classroom.

The programme particularly encourages projects that:

  • Introduce middle school students to citizen science or environmental monitoring activities.
  • Build the capacity of formal and informal educators to provide high-quality STEM programming aligned with state education standards.
  • Help schools develop a culture that uses the environment to improve student learning and achievement.
  • Engage young people in environmental monitoring and the collection of environmental data.
  • Give students opportunities to work with data relating to issues such as air, soil or water quality.
  • Develop Science and Engineering Practices, Disciplinary Core Ideas and Crosscutting Concepts.
  • Build partnerships between schools and community-based organizations.
  • Encourage authentic problem-solving, collaboration and student leadership.
  • Increase student interest in STEM subjects and careers.

Grant Amount

Each selected project will receive:

$5,000

The programme anticipates $25,000 in total funding for the fall 2026 grant cycle, supporting five $5,000 grants. Grantees are expected to complete their Greening STEM projects by spring 2027.

Funding may support eligible project expenses including:

  • Staff and personnel costs for partner project teams
  • Direct travel costs for project team members
  • Transportation for students and youth participants
  • Training and educational materials
  • Project-specific supplies and materials
  • Measurement equipment
  • Tablets and software
  • Data-quality measures and evaluations
  • Professional development for educators and partner staff
  • On-site project costs
  • Postage and shipping
  • Laboratory analysis of air, soil or water samples
  • Data analysis
  • Training related to programme planning, citizen science and environmental monitoring

The source states that no more than 10% of the project budget should support training.

Eligibility

The grant competition is open to public schools serving Grades 6–12 and their community partners located in the following targeted communities:

  • Houston, Texas
  • Corpus Christi–Victoria–Matagorda, Texas
  • Lake Charles, Louisiana
  • Edison, New Jersey
  • Morris, Illinois
  • Clinton, Iowa
  • Cincinnati, Ohio

Applicants must submit their applications through the NEEF online grants system.

Greening STEM Project Design Principles

Projects should incorporate the Greening STEM Design Principles, which are based on an interdisciplinary and collaborative approach to STEM education.

The model places students and their interests at the centre of learning while using natural environments and real-world challenges to encourage exploration, problem-solving and environmental stewardship.

Projects should include four key elements:

1. Place-Based Learning

Students should explore a topic, issue or problem through direct experience and collaboration. Community partners and educators can help connect students with relevant opportunities and resources.

2. Three-Dimensional Learning

Students explore an anchoring phenomenon, question existing assumptions, apply STEM practices and connect disciplinary knowledge with real-world events.

3. Project-Based Learning

Students should engage with challenging project work over an extended period while using appropriate tools, techniques and technology. They should also have opportunities to share their findings with audiences beyond the classroom.

4. Community-Based Learning

Students examine environmental issues within their local cultural and community context. Projects should consider local perspectives and how proposed solutions may affect the communities involved.

Project Expectations

Applicants are expected to describe a citizen science or environmental monitoring project and explain the STEM skills students will develop through participation.

The project should include:

  • A series of STEM learning activities.
  • Pre-field activities that prepare students for field experiences.
  • At least one pre-field activity involving a virtual or in-person visit to the participating school by a community partner representative.
  • One or more field visits where students participate in data collection as part of citizen science or environmental monitoring.
  • At least two post-field activities.
  • A post-field activity involving data analysis.
  • A presentation of project findings.

Application Timeline

The application timeline for the 2026–2027 grant cycle is:

  • Late August 2026: Online applications open
  • October 8, 2026: Grant applications due by 11:59 PM Pacific
  • October 2026: Application review and grantee selection
  • Fall 2026: Award announcement and distribution of funding
  • Spring 2027: Grant performance period concludes
  • Spring 2027: Final reports due

Application Deadline

October 8, 2026, at 11:59 PM Pacific Time.

How to Apply

All applications must be submitted through the NEEF online grants portal. Applicants who have previously applied for a NEEF grant should use their existing account, while first-time applicants will need to create an account.

Applicants should develop their proposal around the Greening STEM model and clearly demonstrate how students will participate in environmental investigation, field-based learning, data collection, analysis and presentation.

Applicants can also consult NEEF’s Grant FAQ resources for additional guidance. Questions about the funding opportunity can be directed to Megan Willig at MWillig@NEEFUsa.org. Technical questions can be sent to grants@neefusa.org, using “EEI LYB Greening STEM Grant” as the email subject.

Grant Expectations

Selected grantees are encouraged to work with NEEF’s K-12 Education team during project design and implementation. They are also required to participate in the programme evaluation process, which may involve interviews, observations and other forms of data collection and analysis.

Grantees will also need to submit signed release forms for students, faculty and staff participating in funded programmes. These forms are due within 30 days of launching the first programme activity.

Conclusion

The 2026 Greening STEM Grant provides public schools and community partners in selected LyondellBasell communities with an opportunity to develop hands-on STEM projects connecting students with environmental science and real-world environmental challenges.

With $5,000 available per selected project, the programme can support activities involving environmental monitoring, citizen science, field experiences, data collection, analysis and community-based learning.

Eligible schools and community partners should prepare projects that place students at the centre of the learning process and demonstrate strong connections between STEM education, local environmental issues and community engagement.

item.content:encoded:
Students and recent graduates seeking hands-on experience in national security, intelligence analysis, communications, geospatial technologies, multimedia production, and international affairs now have an exceptional opportunity to join one of the world’s leading conflict research institutions. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) has officially opened applications for its Spring 2027 Internship Program, offering a broad range of specialized internships designed to train the next generation of analysts, communicators, researchers, and policy leaders.

Based in Washington, DC, ISW is internationally recognized for producing open-source intelligence (OSINT), military assessments, geospatial analysis, strategic reports, and communications products that inform policymakers, defense professionals, journalists, and the wider public. Through its internship program, ISW provides students and recent graduates with direct exposure to cutting-edge research, analytical methodologies, and real-world national security challenges.

The program is hosted under The General David H. Petraeus Center for Emerging Leaders and offers opportunities across several fields, including intelligence analysis, communications, multimedia production, cognitive warfare, geospatial intelligence, and regional conflict research.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, with the final deadline set for November 13, 2026.

About the Institute for the Study of War (ISW)

The Institute for the Study of War is a non-profit research organization dedicated to producing accurate, timely, and evidence-based analysis of global conflicts and security issues. ISW’s work focuses on understanding warfare, military operations, foreign policy, information operations, occupation strategies, and geopolitical developments that affect international security.

ISW’s analyses are regularly consulted by:

  • Policymakers
  • Defense institutions
  • Military leaders
  • Journalists
  • Academic researchers
  • International organizations
  • Security professionals

The organization’s commitment to rigorous open-source intelligence analysis has made it one of the most respected institutions in defense and conflict studies.

Interns become active contributors to this mission, working alongside senior analysts and communications experts while receiving mentorship, leadership training, and professional development.

Why Apply for an ISW Internship?

ISW internships offer much more than traditional work experience. Interns participate directly in projects that contribute to real-world policy discussions and global security analysis.

Benefits include:

1. Hands-On Professional Experience

Interns engage in:

  • Open-source intelligence collection
  • Research and analysis
  • Data visualization
  • Mapping and GIS work
  • Strategic communications
  • Multimedia production
  • Social media management
  • Writing and editing
  • Event support

2. Mentorship from Experts

Participants work directly with:

  • Senior intelligence analysts
  • Communications professionals
  • Geospatial specialists
  • Multimedia experts
  • National security researchers

3. Scholarship Support

ISW offers a scholarship program providing:

  • Up to $1,000 monthly living stipend

Scholarship recipients are selected based on:

  • Potential contribution to ISW teams
  • Demonstrated financial need

4. Academic Credit Opportunities

ISW works with universities to help students obtain academic credit where applicable.

5. Career Development

Former interns have:

  • Published research
  • Developed professional portfolios
  • Transitioned into ISW staff positions
  • Advanced into careers in government, academia, communications, research, and international affairs

ISW Spring 2027 Internship Opportunities

ISW is offering internships across multiple departments and research portfolios.

Intelligence and Research Internships

These internships focus on regional security issues and intelligence analysis:

  • China & Taiwan Intelligence Analysis Internship
  • Korean Peninsula Intelligence Analysis Internship
  • Middle East Intelligence Analysis Internship
  • Russia & Ukraine Intelligence Analysis Internship
  • Russia Occupation Research Internship

Interns will:

  • Analyze open-source information
  • Work with foreign language materials
  • Produce intelligence products
  • Support publications and briefings
  • Assist senior analysts

Preferred language skills include:

  • Mandarin
  • Korean
  • Russian
  • Ukrainian
  • Arabic
  • Hebrew
  • Turkish
  • Kurdish
  • Farsi
  • Japanese
  • Taiwanese Hokkien
  • Tagalog

Cognitive Warfare Project Internship

This opportunity focuses on:

  • Information warfare
  • Disinformation studies
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Cognitive security
  • Strategic communications
  • Data analysis

Applicants with interests in:

  • AI
  • Information technology
  • International affairs
  • Media studies
  • Data visualization

are highly encouraged to apply.

Geospatial Intelligence and National Security Technologies Internship

Students interested in:

  • GIS
  • Satellite imagery
  • Mapping
  • Data visualization
  • Remote sensing

will gain practical experience using:

  • ArcGIS
  • GIS platforms
  • Remote sensing tools
  • Mapping technologies

Experience in:

  • SQL
  • Python
  • Arcpy

is an added advantage.

Communications Internship

This internship provides training in:

  • Media relations
  • Digital communications
  • Social media management
  • Writing and editing
  • Content creation
  • Website management
  • Communications strategy

Interns may work across:

  • X
  • LinkedIn
  • Facebook
  • Instagram
  • Bluesky
  • Threads

Competitive applicants are encouraged to submit:

  • Writing samples
  • Editing samples
  • Graphic design portfolios

Multimedia and Video Production Internship

Ideal for students interested in:

  • Video editing
  • Multimedia storytelling
  • Social media content
  • Graphic design
  • Scriptwriting
  • Visual communications

Preferred skills include:

  • Adobe Premiere Pro
  • Adobe Creative Suite
  • Photography
  • Video production
  • Social media content development

Internship Dates

Spring 2027 internships will run:

  • Start Date: January 12, 2027
  • End Date: May 14, 2027

Note: The Russia Occupation Research Internship lists a separate program timeline:

  • Start Date: September 8, 2026
  • End Date: December 11, 2026

Scholarship Details

Selected interns may receive:

  • Up to $1,000 monthly scholarship support

Applicants must submit a separate scholarship application answering:

  1. Why they selected their preferred internship.
  2. Their views on key national security challenges.
  3. Career goals.
  4. Reasons for applying for scholarship support.
  5. Financial circumstances and aid status.

The scholarship is considered taxable income.

Eligibility Requirements

General eligibility includes:

  • Current college students
  • Graduate students
  • Recent graduates

Applicants should possess:

  • Strong writing and communication skills
  • Research abilities
  • Analytical thinking
  • Attention to detail
  • Ability to work independently

Additional technical skills may include:

  • GIS
  • Foreign languages
  • Data visualization

  • Video editing
  • Open-source intelligence research
  • Graphic design

Work Location

Location:

  • Washington, DC, United States

Formats available:

  • In-person

Applicants must:

  • Be physically present in the United States during the internship
  • Be authorized to work in the US

Applicants may need:

  • Resume

Application Deadline

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until November 13, 2026. Early applications are strongly encouraged.

APPLY HERE

Visit HERE to learn more about the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) Spring 2027 Internships.

Conclusion

The Institute for the Study of War Spring 2027 Internship Program offers a rare opportunity for students and recent graduates to gain practical experience at the intersection of national security, intelligence, communications, geospatial technologies, multimedia production, and international affairs. With mentorship from leading experts, opportunities to contribute to influential research, and scholarship support of up to $1,000 per month, ISW provides an outstanding platform for emerging professionals seeking careers in policy, defense, media, research, and global security.

Applicants with strong analytical skills, communication abilities, technical expertise, and a passion for understanding global conflicts should consider applying before the November 13, 2026 deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027 is a professional learning and development opportunity designed for senior civil and public servants who want to strengthen their understanding of artificial intelligence and its growing implications for public-sector policy, strategy, regulation, and service delivery.

Delivered through the Imperial Policy Forum at Imperial College London, the Fellowship combines in-person learning, expert-led sessions, peer engagement, and an individual research project supported by academic mentors. The programme is designed to help participants move beyond theoretical discussions of AI and apply their learning to real policy challenges within their departments and areas of responsibility.

Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027

Artificial intelligence is increasingly influencing how governments approach public services, regulation, infrastructure, healthcare, security, data, and strategic decision-making. For public-sector leaders, understanding both the capabilities and limitations of AI is becoming increasingly important.

The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship provides an opportunity for senior civil and public servants to explore these issues in a structured environment while developing a research project connected to their own professional priorities.

The 2027 Fellowship will run from February to October 2027, with a total duration of nine months. Fellows will combine online learning and activities with in-person days at Imperial College London.

Key Programme Details

  • Programme: Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027
  • Institution: Imperial College London
  • Duration: 9 months
  • Programme dates: February–October 2027
  • Application deadline: Monday, 2 November 2026
  • Location: London and online
  • Format: Individual research project combined with in-person days at Imperial College London
  • Time commitment: Approximately 6–8 hours per month
  • In-person commitment: Four in-person days throughout the year
  • Fee: £1,500, with no VAT added

What Is the Imperial AI Policy Fellowship?

The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship is a bespoke learning and development programme aimed at senior civil and public servants seeking to develop their knowledge of artificial intelligence and understand how it can affect public-sector work.

Rather than focusing exclusively on classroom-based learning, the programme combines structured learning with practical application.

There are two main components.

1. In-Person Learning at Imperial College London

Throughout the Fellowship, participants attend a series of in-person days at Imperial College London.

These sessions are designed to help Fellows:

  • Understand fundamental AI concepts.
  • Examine how AI technologies work and what they are capable of.
  • Consider the implications of AI for public policy.
  • Explore AI-related strategy and regulation.
  • Examine challenges associated with public-sector delivery.
  • Engage with academics and specialists.
  • Discuss ideas and experiences with other Fellows.
  • Reflect on how AI knowledge can be applied to their professional responsibilities.

The sessions include expert-led lectures, workshops, discussions and opportunities for interaction with peers and specialists.

This structure means that participants are not simply learning about AI in the abstract. They are encouraged to think about how emerging technologies relate to actual policy questions and institutional challenges.

2. Individual Research Project

The second major component is an individual research project or guiding question focused on a specific AI policy challenge.

The project is Fellow-led, meaning that it is shaped around the participant’s own policy priorities and professional objectives.

Fellows receive support from one or more academic mentors who provide expert guidance throughout the programme. This allows participants to investigate an issue that is directly relevant to their area of work while benefiting from Imperial’s academic expertise and institutional environment.

The research component is therefore an important bridge between learning and practical policy development.

What Can the Research Project Focus On?

The Fellowship provides flexibility in the type of project participants can develop.

Potential project formats include:

  • Written recommendations for adopting AI within a particular part of a government department.
  • Co-designing strategic plans or technical solutions for policy challenges.
  • Piloting innovative or experimental AI applications within the public sector.
  • Improving systems and infrastructure for AI, including data storage and management.
  • Organising a facilitated workshop for colleagues within a department or team.
  • Producing a published white paper.

This flexibility allows Fellows to connect the Fellowship to real issues they are already encountering in their professional roles.

Examples of Previous Research Projects

The programme provides examples demonstrating how AI policy research can be connected to practical public-sector challenges.

Previous examples include:

AI and Food Regulation

One project involved piloting an AI model for the Food Standards Agency designed to help organisations identify relevant regulations and the bodies responsible for those regulations.

AI, Healthcare and Accountability

Another project involved a paper co-written between the MHRA and NHS examining the accountability gap surrounding clinical negligence, product liability and practitioner literacy within the UK healthcare system.

Human-Centred AI

A collaborative workshop explored human-centred AI design involving the Home Office and Imperial’s Collective Innovation Lab.

AI and Defence

Another example focused on Sovereign AI in Defence, involving Imperial academics, the Trusted AI Alliance and consultation with the UK Ministry of Defence.

These examples illustrate the breadth of potential applications for AI policy research across government and public services.

Benefits of the Imperial AI Policy Fellowship

The Fellowship offers several forms of professional and academic development.

Tailored Learning

The programme provides a personalised learning experience based on Fellows’ individual needs and professional interests.

This allows participants to focus their learning on issues that are relevant to their roles rather than following a completely generic AI curriculum.

Practical Research Experience

Fellows undertake a research project supported by an academic mentor.

This provides an opportunity to apply AI knowledge to a real policy question and develop practical outputs that can potentially be useful within their departments.

Access to Imperial Expertise

Participants have the opportunity to learn from faculty and specialists associated with Imperial College London, including experts working across AI-related areas in engineering, medicine and science.

Professional Networking

The Fellowship brings together civil servants and public-sector professionals who share an interest in AI and related policy challenges.

Participants can exchange experiences, develop professional relationships and learn from colleagues working on different policy issues.

Public-Sector Focus

The programme is specifically designed around the challenges of applying AI within the public sector.

This means Fellows can explore questions involving policy, governance, regulation, strategy, implementation and public-sector systems rather than concentrating solely on the technical development of AI.

Engagement with the Wider Imperial Community

Fellows will also have opportunities to engage with the Imperial Policy Forum and the wider Imperial community.

The programme combines these connections with formal learning and individual research, creating an environment in which participants can develop their understanding of AI while applying that knowledge to current policy questions.

The Fellowship’s activities have also included engagement with Imperial’s AI and technology ecosystem. The programme information highlights Fellows visiting Imperial’s biomedical engineering facilities and participating in workshops involving AI startups at the Deep Tech White City campus.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The programme is intended for senior civil and public servants who want to deepen their understanding of AI and its implications for public-sector work.

It is particularly relevant to professionals who:

  • Work on policy development or implementation.
  • Have responsibilities involving technology or digital transformation.
  • Work with AI-related regulation or governance.
  • Are responsible for strategic planning.
  • Work in public-sector innovation.
  • Need to understand the implications of AI for their department.
  • Want to investigate a specific AI-related policy challenge.
  • Are interested in developing an evidence-based project connected to AI and public policy.

The supplied programme information does not provide a specific nationality, race, or continent-based eligibility restriction. Therefore, those details should not be assumed from the available information.

Time Commitment

The Fellowship runs for nine months and requires approximately 6–8 hours per month.

Participants must also commit to four in-person days throughout the year. The programme therefore combines ongoing engagement with concentrated periods of face-to-face learning at Imperial College London.

Where Is the Fellowship Held?

The Fellowship uses a hybrid format.

Participants engage through:

  • Online activities.
  • In-person sessions.
  • Individual research.
  • Engagement with Imperial’s academic and policy communities.

The programme location is listed as London and online, with in-person days taking place at Imperial College London.

Fellowship Cost

The fee for participation in the 2027 Imperial AI Policy Fellowship is:

£1,500

The programme information states that no VAT is added to this fee.

Application Deadline

Applications for the 2027 Fellowship are currently open.

The application deadline is:

Monday, 2 November 2026

Applicants are instructed to complete the application form and send it to the Imperial Policy Forum at the.forum@imperial.ac.uk.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their application materials are completed and submitted before the stated deadline.

How to Apply

Prospective applicants should:

  1. Review the Imperial AI Policy Fellowship programme information.
  2. Consider how AI relates to their current public-sector responsibilities.
  3. Identify a policy challenge or research question that could form the basis of their Fellowship project.
  4. Consider what they hope to gain from the programme.
  5. Complete the official application form.
  6. Submit the completed application to the Imperial Policy Forum before the deadline.

The official programme page provides access to both the programme brochure and the 2027 application form.

Learn more and apply HERE

Why the Research Project Matters

A distinctive feature of this Fellowship is that participants are not simply passive recipients of training.

The research project gives each Fellow an opportunity to connect their learning to a real-world policy challenge.

For example, a participant could investigate how their department might adopt AI responsibly, explore policy requirements for a new technology, examine AI-related data infrastructure, develop recommendations for senior decision-makers, or design a workshop to improve colleagues’ understanding of AI.

The project can therefore become a practical mechanism for transferring learning from the Fellowship into the Fellow’s professional environment.

A Fellowship Focused on Practical AI Policy

The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship sits at the intersection of artificial intelligence, public policy and government leadership.

As governments and public institutions consider how AI should be adopted, regulated and governed, public-sector professionals increasingly need the ability to understand both the opportunities and challenges associated with the technology.

The Fellowship’s structure responds to this need by combining:

  • AI fundamentals.
  • Policy analysis.
  • Expert learning.
  • Academic mentorship.
  • Practical research.
  • Peer exchange.
  • Professional networking.
  • Public-sector application.

This combination allows Fellows to explore AI from both technical and policy perspectives while maintaining a strong connection to their professional responsibilities.

Key Dates and Facts at a Glance

Detail Information
Programme Imperial AI Policy Fellowship
Entry 2027
Institution Imperial College London
Duration 9 months
Programme period February–October 2027
Deadline 2 November 2026
Location London and online
In-person commitment 4 days
Monthly time commitment 6–8 hours
Fee £1,500
Main participants Senior civil and public servants
Main focus AI, public policy and public-sector applications
Research component Individual Fellow-led project
Academic support One or more academic mentors

The programme details above are based on the supplied Imperial College London programme information.

Conclusion

The Imperial AI Policy Fellowship 2027 provides a structured opportunity for senior civil and public servants to deepen their understanding of artificial intelligence and examine how it can be applied to contemporary public-sector challenges.

Running for nine months from February to October 2027, the programme combines in-person learning at Imperial College London, online engagement, expert-led sessions, peer networking and a Fellow-led research project supported by academic mentors. Participants can use the research component to explore practical questions involving AI adoption, policy development, regulation, public-sector systems, strategy and governance.

With applications closing on 2 November 2026, prospective applicants should review the programme requirements, identify a relevant policy challenge and prepare their application well before the deadline.

For more opportunities click HERE

item.content:encoded:
The Global Innovation Fellowships: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace 2026 provide an exciting opportunity for early- and mid-career researchers based in the United Kingdom to expand their professional networks, strengthen their research and policy engagement skills, and develop innovative responses to some of the world’s most complex challenges.

Offered by the British Academy in partnership with the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, the fellowship is designed for researchers working across the humanities and social sciences who want to build stronger connections between academia, policymaking, and professional practice.

The programme provides successful fellows with the opportunity to become embedded within the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace for a period of 12 months, with placements based in Washington, DC, Singapore, or Beirut, depending on the thematic area and proposed fellowship.

With awards of up to £150,000 for 12 months, the Global Innovation Fellowships are intended to support researchers in developing new ideas, building international networks, translating academic knowledge into practical applications, and contributing fresh perspectives to policy challenges.

The fellowship is particularly relevant to researchers interested in international affairs, global governance, climate and sustainability, geopolitics, Asian regional affairs, the Middle East and North Africa, international institutions, and other interconnected global challenges.

Global Innovation Fellowships 2026 Overview

The Global Innovation Fellowships are part of the British Academy’s efforts to support researchers in the humanities and social sciences in developing relationships beyond traditional academic environments.

The programme seeks to create opportunities where researchers can work directly with organisations operating in policy and practice. Through this approach, fellows can gain exposure to different perspectives and working environments while also contributing their academic expertise to real-world challenges.

Key details of the 2026 fellowship include:

  • Fellowship: Global Innovation Fellowships: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace
  • Host organisation: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace
  • Funding organisation: British Academy
  • Career stage: Early-career and mid-career researchers
  • Application status: Open for applications
  • Opening date: 22 September 2026
  • Application deadline: 18 November 2026 at 17:00 GMT
  • Interview date: 8 February 2027
  • Expected commencement: By September 2027
  • Possible earlier commencement: March or April 2027
  • Duration: 12 months
  • Maximum award: Up to £150,000
  • Number of fellowships: Up to two
  • Potential host locations: Washington, DC; Singapore; or Beirut
  • Applicant location requirement: United Kingdom
  • Academic disciplines: Humanities and social sciences
  • Contact: international@thebritishacademy.ac.uk

About the Global Innovation Fellowships

The British Academy has received funding from the UK Department of Business, Innovation, Science and Trade to support its Innovation Fellowships programme.

The Global Innovation Fellowships are intended to help researchers develop their skills, professional networks, and careers outside conventional academic environments. The programme places particular emphasis on creating connections between researchers and organisations in the creative and cultural, public, private, and policy sectors.

The fellowship recognises that many of today’s major challenges cannot be addressed effectively through a single discipline or institution. Issues such as climate change, sustainability, international security, geopolitical competition, global governance, technology, and regional political and economic transformation often require multiple perspectives.

The programme therefore encourages researchers to bring their academic knowledge into a different professional setting while learning from practitioners, policymakers, and other experts.

Partnership with the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace

The fourth call of the Global Innovation Fellowships provides opportunities for selected award holders to become embedded within the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace.

Carnegie is an international foreign policy institution whose experts work across different disciplines and regions on major global issues. Its work covers areas including democracy, technology, climate change, international affairs, and regional geopolitical developments.

The fellowship is therefore structured to expose successful researchers to an environment where academic knowledge, policy analysis, international engagement, and practical problem-solving intersect.

Depending on the subject of the fellowship, researchers may be hosted in Washington, DC, Singapore, or Beirut, with opportunities to engage with Carnegie colleagues and regional programmes.

Main Objectives of the Fellowship

The Global Innovation Fellowships are designed around a mutually beneficial relationship between the award holder and Carnegie.

For fellows, the programme can provide an opportunity to:

  • Develop new professional networks beyond academia.
  • Strengthen connections with policymakers and practitioners.
  • Translate academic research and expertise into practical applications.
  • Develop innovative approaches to policy challenges.
  • Gain experience working within an international policy organisation.
  • Explore new perspectives on complex global issues.
  • Strengthen professional skills relevant to policy and practice.
  • Build relationships with experts working in different regions and disciplines.
  • Increase the practical reach and impact of their research.
  • Develop new collaborations that may continue beyond the fellowship.
  • Improve their ability to communicate academic knowledge to non-academic audiences.

For Carnegie, the fellowship provides an opportunity to benefit from the expertise, perspectives, research approaches, and experiences of researchers from the UK humanities and social sciences community.

Research Areas for the 2026 Fellowship

Applicants are invited to submit proposals in one of four broad thematic areas.

1. Sustainability, Climate and Geopolitics

The first thematic area focuses on the interconnected challenges associated with climate change, sustainability, and nature.

A fellowship in this area would be based in Washington, DC and would examine the relationship between environmental challenges and broader geopolitical developments.

Applicants could explore issues surrounding the changing global environment, sustainability challenges, climate-related risks, geopolitical consequences, and innovative approaches to addressing interconnected environmental and international problems.

The theme recognises that climate and sustainability challenges are not isolated environmental issues. They can intersect with economics, international relations, security, development, governance, resources, and global cooperation.

2. Global Order and Institutions

The second thematic area focuses on questions surrounding global order, disorder, and international institutions.

This fellowship would also be based in Washington, DC.

Applicants working in this area could investigate different dimensions of the international system, including the functioning and evolution of international institutions, changing global relationships, international cooperation, and the challenges facing existing structures of global governance.

The programme notes that there is no single solution to the challenges associated with global order and disorder. Applicants are therefore expected to bring thoughtful perspectives and potentially innovative approaches to understanding these developments.

3. South and East Asia

The third thematic area focuses on South Asia, East Asia, and Southeast Asia.

A fellowship in this area could be based in either Washington, DC, or Singapore, depending on the proposed work and engagement with Carnegie counterparts.

Applicants should have strong expertise in one or more of these regions, including expertise relating to India or China and their regional or global roles.

The programme is particularly interested in researchers who can contribute informed perspectives on the political, economic, social, strategic, and international dimensions of developments in these regions.

Researchers may also engage with questions concerning the broader role of South and East Asian countries in international affairs.

4. Middle East and North Africa

The fourth thematic area focuses on the Middle East and North Africa (MENA).

Fellows in this area would work with Carnegie’s Middle East Program and could be based in Washington, DC, or Beirut.

The fellowship may involve examining major challenges facing the region, long-term geopolitical trends, and possible innovative policy approaches.

Applicants should have relevant expertise in the Middle East and North Africa, including the Gulf and Iran.

The programme welcomes applicants with particular country or thematic expertise relating to political, social, or economic change.

Academic and Professional Background

The Global Innovation Fellowships do not prescribe one particular academic discipline.

Applicants may come from a broad range of disciplinary, conceptual, and methodological backgrounds. The programme is open to perspectives that may be analytical, policy-oriented, practical, or combinations of these approaches.

However, applicants must demonstrate a strong understanding of the issues relevant to their proposed fellowship, including the applicable policy environment and the systemic challenges associated with the subject.

This means that applicants should be able to demonstrate more than academic interest in their chosen area. They should be able to explain the wider policy context and show how their expertise can contribute to understanding or addressing the challenges involved.

Relevant language skills can be beneficial where appropriate to the proposed research or regional focus, although language skills are desirable rather than mandatory.

Who Can Apply for the Global Innovation Fellowships?

The programme is specifically designed for UK-based early- and mid-career researchers.

To be eligible, applicants must meet several important conditions.

UK Residency

Applicants must be ordinarily resident in the United Kingdom.

This requirement means that the fellowship is not a general worldwide opportunity open to researchers residing in any country.

Current Long-Term Appointment

Applicants must have a current long-term appointment that will continue for at least the duration of the fellowship award.

The applicant must also be based at an eligible UK institution, such as:

  • A Higher Education Institution (HEI); or
  • An Independent Research Organisation (IRO).

The institution must be listed as an approving organisation within the British Academy’s Flexi-Grant system.

If an applicant is successful, the institution will be issued the relevant terms and conditions associated with the award.

Career Stage

The fellowship is intended for:

  • Early-career researchers; and
  • Mid-career researchers.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate an established connection to research as well as a clear rationale for how the fellowship will contribute to their professional development and future career.

Humanities and Social Sciences

Applicants should be researchers working within disciplines in the humanities and social sciences that are eligible under the British Academy’s grant management system.

There is no single required disciplinary background. The programme allows applicants to approach the thematic areas from different academic, methodological, conceptual, analytical, policy, and practical perspectives.

Who Is Not Eligible?

Postgraduate students are not eligible to apply for British Academy grant support under this programme.

Applicants must confirm that they are not:

  • Currently working towards a PhD;
  • Awaiting the outcome of a viva voce examination; or
  • Awaiting acceptance of corrections required by examiners.

This is an important requirement for applicants who have recently completed or are close to completing doctoral studies.

Applicants should carefully assess their status against these requirements before beginning an application.

Collaboration Between Academia and Policy

One of the central features of the Global Innovation Fellowships is the emphasis on moving knowledge between academic and non-academic environments.

The fellowship is not simply intended to provide researchers with another academic research placement. Instead, successful applicants are expected to demonstrate how engagement with Carnegie can create value for both sides.

Applicants should consider:

  • How their academic expertise can contribute to Carnegie’s work.
  • What they can learn from working within a policy-focused organisation.
  • How collaboration can generate new ideas.
  • How their research can be translated into policy-relevant knowledge.
  • How interaction with practitioners can influence their future work.
  • How they can develop new professional networks.
  • How their experience can contribute to their long-term career development.

The programme particularly seeks applicants who are willing to explore perspectives outside their established academic environment.

What the Fellowship Looks for in Applicants

Successful applicants are expected to demonstrate an openness to new ideas and a willingness to experiment with innovative approaches.

Important qualities include:

  • Intellectual openness.
  • Willingness to explore new perspectives.
  • Interest in interdisciplinary engagement.
  • Ability to work across academic and non-academic environments.
  • Commitment to challenge-driven work.
  • Interest in policy and practice.
  • Ability to engage constructively with different perspectives.
  • Understanding of the needs and priorities of the partner organisation.
  • A clear interest in knowledge mobilisation and translation.
  • A strong connection between the proposed fellowship and future professional development.

Applicants should therefore carefully explain not only what they want to research or explore, but also why working with Carnegie is particularly valuable to their proposed project and professional trajectory.

Fellowship Locations

The location of the fellowship will depend largely on the thematic area and the nature of the proposed work.

Possible locations include:

Washington, DC

Washington, DC is the proposed location for fellowships focusing on:

  • Sustainability, climate and geopolitics.
  • Global order and institutions.
  • Some work related to South and East Asia.
  • Some work related to the Middle East and North Africa.

Singapore

Singapore may host fellows working on South and East Asian issues.

This provides an opportunity for researchers to engage with regional perspectives and Carnegie counterparts working on Asia.

Beirut

Beirut may host fellows working on Middle East and North Africa issues through Carnegie’s Middle East Program.

The location is therefore closely connected to the applicant’s thematic expertise and proposed area of engagement.

Fellowship Value and Financial Support

The British Academy is offering up to two fellowships, each lasting up to 12 months.

Each award can be worth up to £150,000.

The awards are offered with Full Economic Costing at 80 percent.

The financial support is intended to facilitate a substantial period of engagement with Carnegie and enable successful researchers to undertake the fellowship in an international policy environment.

Applicants should carefully consult the official scheme guidance to understand the eligible costs, institutional arrangements, funding conditions, and other financial requirements associated with the award.

Fellowship Duration and Start Date

The Global Innovation Fellowships are expected to commence by September 2027.

However, an earlier start in March or April 2027 may be possible.

Applicants seeking an earlier start date will need to explain how they intend to manage the relocation process within the shorter preparation period.

The standard fellowship duration is 12 months.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Global Innovation Fellowships 2026 is:

18 November 2026 at 17:00 GMT

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications. It is advisable to review the scheme guidance, eligibility requirements, institutional requirements, and application materials well in advance of the deadline.

Interview Date

Applicants should also take note of the planned interview date.

Interviews are scheduled for 8 February 2027.

Applicants should ensure that they are available during this period if invited to an interview.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants interested in the Global Innovation Fellowships should carefully consider how their expertise, proposed area of work, and career objectives align with the programme.

A strong application should clearly establish the connection between the applicant’s background and the fellowship theme.

Applicants should consider addressing the following areas:

1. Clearly Identify the Relevant Thematic Area

Determine whether the proposed fellowship fits within:

  • Sustainability, Climate and Geopolitics;
  • Global Order and Institutions;
  • South and East Asia; or
  • Middle East and North Africa.

The proposal should demonstrate a clear connection to the selected theme.

2. Demonstrate Relevant Expertise

Applicants should explain their expertise and experience in the relevant area.

This may include academic research, publications, policy engagement, professional experience, regional knowledge, methodological expertise, or practical work.

3. Explain the Policy Context

The programme expects applicants to have a solid understanding of the relevant policy landscape.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate awareness of the wider systems, institutions, actors, challenges, and policy debates connected to their proposed area.

4. Explain Why Carnegie

Applicants should clearly explain why the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace is an appropriate partner for their proposed fellowship.

The application should demonstrate how engagement with Carnegie could create opportunities for:

  • Knowledge exchange.
  • Collaboration.
  • Professional development.
  • Policy engagement.
  • New research perspectives.
  • Network development.
  • Innovative approaches to complex challenges.

5. Demonstrate Value Beyond Academia

Applicants should explain how their proposed fellowship could strengthen interaction between academic research and non-academic environments.

This could involve showing how research findings might be translated into policy-relevant knowledge or how practical engagement could inform future academic work.

6. Connect the Fellowship to Career Development

Applicants should demonstrate how the fellowship fits into their longer-term professional development.

The programme is intended to help researchers develop skills, networks, and careers, so applicants should clearly explain what they expect to gain and how the experience could contribute to their future work.

Important Eligibility Considerations

Before applying, prospective applicants should carefully review the official scheme guidance.

Particular attention should be paid to:

  • UK residency requirements.
  • Employment and appointment requirements.
  • Eligible UK institutions.
  • Career-stage requirements.
  • Eligible disciplinary backgrounds.
  • Postgraduate student restrictions.
  • Current British Academy award restrictions.
  • Carnegie’s requirements for working at and with the organisation.
  • Fellowship location and relocation considerations.
  • The relationship between the proposed work and the selected thematic area.

Applicants may not hold more than one British Academy award of a comparable nature at the same time.

Previous Global Innovation Fellowship Awards

The 2026 call represents the fourth call under this programme.

Previous award holders and their projects are available through the British Academy’s Global Innovation Fellowships past awards information. Reviewing previous awards can help prospective applicants understand the types of projects and approaches that have previously been supported.

However, applicants should use previous awards as a source of context rather than attempting to replicate earlier projects. The current call has its own thematic areas, requirements, and application criteria.

Why the Fellowship Is Relevant to Researchers

The Global Innovation Fellowships offer researchers an opportunity to move beyond conventional academic boundaries and engage directly with an international policy organisation.

For researchers whose work intersects with global affairs, international institutions, climate, sustainability, geopolitics, Asian regional affairs, or Middle Eastern and North African affairs, the programme provides an environment for developing connections between research and policy.

The fellowship can also help researchers develop the ability to communicate complex academic ideas to audiences outside universities.

This knowledge mobilisation and translation dimension is particularly important because research can have greater practical relevance when it is effectively communicated to policymakers, practitioners, institutions, and other stakeholders.

Application Process

Interested researchers should begin by reviewing the official fellowship guidance and eligibility requirements before accessing the application system.

The general process involves:

  1. Reviewing the official Global Innovation Fellowships scheme information.
  2. Confirming eligibility.
  3. Identifying the most appropriate thematic area.
  4. Developing a clear fellowship proposal.
  5. Discussing the application with the relevant UK institution where appropriate.
  6. Reviewing the requirements for working with Carnegie.
  7. Preparing the required application information and supporting materials.
  8. Completing the application through the British Academy’s application system.
  9. Submitting the completed application before the deadline.
  10. Preparing for the interview stage if shortlisted.

Applicants should allow sufficient time for institutional processes and final application checks.

APPLY HERE

Official Application and Further Information

Applications are submitted through the British Academy’s grant application system.

Applicants should also read the official scheme guidance notes and frequently asked questions before submitting an application. These resources provide additional information about eligibility, application requirements, the fellowship arrangement, and other programme conditions.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Global Innovation Fellowships.

Conclusion

The Global Innovation Fellowships: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace 2026 provide UK-based early- and mid-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences with an opportunity to develop their professional networks, strengthen policy engagement, and explore innovative approaches to major international challenges.

The programme offers up to two 12-month fellowships, with awards of up to £150,000, and placements potentially based in Washington, DC, Singapore, or Beirut. The four thematic areas cover sustainability, climate and geopolitics; global order and institutions; South and East Asia; and the Middle East and North Africa.

Because eligibility is specifically focused on researchers ordinarily resident in the UK and holding qualifying long-term appointments at eligible UK institutions, prospective applicants should carefully confirm their status before preparing an application.

Researchers who meet the requirements and can demonstrate relevant expertise, openness to interdisciplinary perspectives, interest in policy engagement, and a clear rationale for working with Carnegie should review the official scheme guidance and prepare their applications well ahead of the 18 November 2026, 17:00 GMT deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Oxford Farming Conference (OFC) Scholars Programme 2027 is now preparing to welcome a new group of young people to one of the UK’s leading agricultural conferences, offering participants an opportunity to develop professional skills, build valuable networks and engage directly with leaders and emerging voices across agriculture, food, business, science, technology and related sectors.

The 2027 programme is particularly significant because it marks 25 years since the OFC Scholars Programme began. For its 2027 edition, the programme is being delivered in partnership with Severn Trent Water and M&S, introducing a hybrid programme combining in-person gatherings, online learning and participation in the live Oxford Farming Conference in January 2027.

Importantly, the programme is not restricted to people who have studied agriculture or currently work within the farming sector. OFC says it welcomes individuals from non-traditional sectors and backgrounds, as well as people with diverse geographical and academic experiences. Applicants who have never studied an agri-food subject are also encouraged to be considered.

The programme is designed to help develop the future generations of agricultural and related-sector leaders, while giving Scholars access to peer networking, skills development, professional exposure and the opportunity to participate in discussions surrounding the future of agriculture.

What Is the Oxford Farming Conference Scholars Programme?

The Oxford Farming Conference (OFC) Scholars Programme is an initiative designed to support and develop young people who have the potential to contribute to the future of agriculture and related industries.

Rather than simply providing conference attendance, the programme combines the main OFC conference experience with a wider programme of learning and networking activities.

The 2027 programme will use a hybrid model, meaning Scholars will participate through a mixture of:

  • In-person professional and educational events.
  • Online bespoke sessions.
  • Peer-to-peer networking.
  • Skills development activities.
  • The live Oxford Farming Conference.
  • Exposure to people and organisations involved in agriculture and associated sectors.

The programme is intended to provide participants with an opportunity to exchange ideas and perspectives while developing practical skills that can support their future careers and leadership ambitions.

Oxford Farming Conference Scholars Programme 2027 Highlights

The 2027 programme offers a number of significant benefits to successful Scholars.

Key features include:

  • Participation in the Oxford Farming Conference 2027.
  • Full conference access.
  • Two nights of accommodation.
  • Meals associated with the conference programme.
  • Attendance at the Chair’s Welcome Reception.
  • Participation in the Oxford Union Debate.
  • Attendance at the Christ Church dinner.
  • Two dedicated in-person development and networking events.
  • Bespoke online webinars.
  • Peer-to-peer networking opportunities.
  • Skills development training.
  • Exposure to agricultural and food-sector leaders.
  • Opportunities to meet people from different professional, geographical and academic backgrounds.
  • The opportunity to become part of the OFC Scholars community.

The programme is limited to a defined number of participants, making the application and selection process competitive.

How Many Scholars Will Be Selected?

For the standard Scholars Programme, 22 individuals will be selected.

These places are funded by individual sponsors, who must nominate a proposed Scholar through the application process.

In addition to the 22 standard Scholar places, the 2027 programme will include 8 Breaking Barriers places.

The Breaking Barriers places are being funded by OFC, Severn Trent Water and M&S and have a separate application arrangement.

This means the 2027 programme is designed to provide opportunities for a broader range of young people, including individuals who may not traditionally have had access to major agricultural conferences or professional networks.

Previous Oxford Farming Conference Attendance

Applicants must also not have previously attended the Oxford Farming Conference.

The Scholars Programme is intended to introduce new participants to the conference and provide them with an opportunity to experience OFC for the first time.

Therefore, someone who has previously attended the Oxford Farming Conference would not meet the stated requirement for the standard Scholars Programme.

Do You Need an Agriculture Degree to Apply?

No specific agricultural academic qualification is stated as a requirement.

This is one of the programme’s key features.

OFC explicitly encourages applications from people who have not studied agri-food subjects and says the programme welcomes individuals from outside the agriculture sector.

This means that people with backgrounds in areas such as business, technology, science, policy, environmental studies, communications, economics, engineering and other disciplines may potentially be relevant to the programme, provided they meet the stated requirements and are put forward through the appropriate application route.

The emphasis is therefore broader than academic agricultural qualifications alone.

Who Can Sponsor a Scholar?

The standard Scholars Programme uses a sponsor-led application model.

According to OFC, any sponsor, organisation or group can apply for a Scholar place.

The application must identify the proposed Scholar and provide information explaining:

  1. Who the proposed Scholar is.
  2. Their background and experience.
  3. Why they are suitable for the opportunity.
  4. How they are expected to benefit from participating in the programme.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to organisations, businesses, professional groups and other bodies that want to support the development of a promising young person.

How Does the Sponsorship and Funding Process Work?

The standard Scholar places are fully funded by the applicant/sponsor.

Sponsors submit an application on behalf of their proposed Scholar.

The applications are then reviewed by the OFC Directors, with successful candidates offered a place on the programme.

Importantly, a place is not confirmed until payment has been received.

After an application is successful, the sponsoring organisation, group or individual will receive information about registration and payment.

How Much Does the OFC Scholars Programme Cost?

The cost of a Scholar place for OFC 2027 is:

£1,000 excluding VAT

The £1,000 cost includes a substantial package of conference-related benefits.

According to the programme information, this includes:

  • Two nights’ accommodation.
  • The Chair’s Welcome Reception.
  • The Oxford Union Debate.
  • The iconic Christ Church dinner.
  • Conference participation and associated Scholar activities.

Travel costs are not included

Sponsors should be aware that travel expenses are not included in the £1,000 fee.

Additional funding should therefore be set aside for travel associated with:

  • The in-person Scholar events.
  • The January 2027 Oxford Farming Conference.

Sponsors are expected to liaise directly with their Scholars regarding travel costs and reimbursement arrangements.

OFC Scholars Programme 2027 Schedule

The 2027 programme includes several stages, beginning with applications in September 2026 and culminating in the Oxford Farming Conference in January 2027.

Here is the announced timetable:

Activity Date
Applications Open Thursday, 17 September 2026
Applications Close Friday, 16 October 2026
Application Shortlisting by OFC Week commencing 19 October 2026
Candidates Notified Week commencing 26 October 2026
First In-Person Event: Supply Chain Day in London 12 November 2026
Second In-Person Event: Primary Production Day at Harper Adams, Shropshire 25 November 2026
Online Webinars Between 12 November and 12 December 2026
OFC 2027 6–8 January 2027

The dates for the online webinars will be confirmed with successful candidates.

Breaking Barriers additional event

Breaking Barriers participants have an additional gathering scheduled for:

24 November 2026

Application Deadline for the OFC Scholars Programme 2027

The stated application deadline is:

5pm on Friday, 16 October 2026

Applicants and sponsoring organisations should ensure that applications are submitted before the stated closing time.

Important: The supplied programme information contains one reference to “16th October 2027” when describing the application deadline, but the programme schedule and the rest of the announcement identify the deadline as Friday, 16 October 2026. Since applications open in September 2026 and shortlisting takes place in October 2026, 16 October 2026 appears to be the intended deadline.

Prospective applicants should nevertheless verify the deadline on the official OFC application page before submitting.

What Happens After Applications Close?

After applications close, the Oxford Farming Conference Directors will review the submitted applications.

The announced selection process is:

1. Applications close

Applications must be submitted by the stated deadline of 5pm on Friday, 16 October 2026.

2. OFC reviews applications

The OFC Directors will shortlist applications during the week commencing 19 October 2026.

3. Candidates are notified

Applicants are expected to be notified during the week commencing 26 October 2026.

4. Successful Scholars participate in the programme

Successful Scholars will then begin taking part in the scheduled programme of in-person events, online sessions and the January conference.

First In-Person Scholar Event: Supply Chain Day in London

The first major in-person Scholar gathering is scheduled for:

12 November 2026

This event will be a Supply Chain Day in London.

It forms part of the programme’s broader objective of exposing Scholars to different aspects of the agricultural and food system.

The supply chain perspective is particularly relevant to a programme that seeks to attract participants from diverse sectors rather than focusing exclusively on primary agricultural production.

Second In-Person Scholar Event: Primary Production Day

The second in-person event will take place on:

25 November 2026

at Harper Adams University in Shropshire.

This will be a Primary Production Day, giving Scholars another perspective on the agricultural system.

Together, the London Supply Chain Day and Harper Adams Primary Production Day are intended to give participants exposure to different parts of the agricultural and food landscape.

Online Webinars

Alongside the physical gatherings, Scholars will have access to bespoke online sessions.

The online webinars will be hosted between:

12 November and 12 December 2026

The precise schedule will be confirmed with successful candidates.

These online sessions are part of the hybrid structure of the 2027 programme and provide additional opportunities for learning, discussion and engagement without requiring participants to travel for every activity.

Attending the Oxford Farming Conference 2027

The main event of the programme will be the Oxford Farming Conference 2027, taking place from:

6–8 January 2027

Successful Scholars will attend the live conference in Oxford as part of their programme.

This gives Scholars the opportunity to experience one of the UK’s major agricultural conferences while connecting with other delegates, speakers, professionals and sector leaders.

The conference experience is combined with the wider Scholar development programme, making the opportunity more than simply a conference ticket.

What Does the OFC 2027 Conference Experience Include?

The Scholar package includes access to several important conference activities.

These include:

  • The Chair’s Welcome Reception.
  • The Oxford Union Debate.
  • The Christ Church dinner.
  • Two nights of accommodation.
  • Conference participation.
  • Other activities included within the Scholar programme.

The programme is therefore structured to provide Scholars with both professional development and social/networking opportunities during their time at OFC.

Breaking Barriers Places

In addition to the 22 standard Scholar places, the 2027 programme includes 8 Breaking Barriers places.

These places are being funded by:

  • Oxford Farming Conference.
  • Severn Trent Water.
  • M&S.

The Breaking Barriers programme has a dedicated application route, meaning people interested in this pathway should follow the specific Breaking Barriers application instructions rather than assuming that the standard sponsor-led process applies.

Breaking Barriers participants will also have an additional gathering on:

24 November 2026.

The announcement indicates that further information about the Breaking Barriers route is provided in its dedicated section.

Why the Programme Is Significant for Young Professionals

The OFC Scholars Programme is designed around more than attendance at a single conference.

It provides participants with a structured opportunity to:

  1. Develop professional skills.
  2. Build relationships with peers.
  3. Engage with people from different backgrounds.
  4. Gain exposure to the agricultural supply chain.
  5. Learn about primary production.
  6. Participate in online learning sessions.
  7. Attend a major agricultural conference.
  8. Experience professional networking in a high-level conference environment.
  9. Exchange ideas and perspectives with other emerging professionals.
  10. Develop relationships that may support future leadership and career development.

The programme’s willingness to welcome people from outside traditional agricultural backgrounds also makes it relevant to individuals working at the intersection of agriculture with other disciplines and industries.

Can Someone From Outside Agriculture Apply?

Yes.

This is explicitly encouraged.

OFC states that the programme welcomes people from outside the agriculture sector, including individuals who have not studied agri-food subjects.

This is particularly relevant for young professionals whose work intersects with agriculture without being traditionally classified as agricultural employment.

For example, individuals working in related areas could potentially bring perspectives from their own disciplines into discussions about the future of agriculture and food systems.

What Sponsors Need to Know

Organisations or groups considering supporting a young person through the programme should pay attention to several important points.

Sponsorship requirements

The sponsor must:

  • Submit the application.
  • Name the proposed Scholar.
  • Explain who the individual is.
  • Explain how the individual would benefit from the programme.
  • Fund the Scholar place if the application is successful.
  • Consider additional travel funding.

Programme cost

The standard cost is:

£1,000 + VAT per Scholar.

Travel

Travel expenses are not included.

Sponsors should therefore budget separately for travel to the two away-day events and the January 2027 conference.

Confirmation

A successful application does not become a confirmed place until the required payment has been received.

Key Dates at a Glance

For easy reference, prospective applicants and sponsors should note the following dates:

17 September 2026 — Applications open.

16 October 2026 at 5pm — Applications close.

Week commencing 19 October 2026 — OFC shortlisting.

Week commencing 26 October 2026 — Candidates notified.

12 November 2026 — Supply Chain Day in London.

24 November 2026 — Additional Breaking Barriers gathering.

25 November 2026 — Primary Production Day at Harper Adams, Shropshire.

12 November–12 December 2026 — Online webinars.

6–8 January 2027 — Oxford Farming Conference 2027.

6 January 2027, 1pm–1:30pm — Optional familiarisation session for first-time delegates.

How to Apply for the OFC Scholars Programme 2027

The application process depends on which part of the programme an applicant is seeking to access.

For the standard Scholars Programme, a sponsor, organisation or group must submit an application naming the proposed Scholar.

The application should demonstrate who the individual is and explain how participation in the programme would benefit them.

The application is then reviewed by the OFC Directors.

APPLY HERE

For the Breaking Barriers route, applicants should use the dedicated Breaking Barriers application process because it operates separately from the standard sponsor-led route.

Prospective applicants should use the official OFC application information and carefully check the relevant instructions before submitting an application.

Application deadline: 5pm, Friday 16 October 2026.

Read Full Details About This Opportunity HERE

What Successful Scholars Can Expect

A successful Scholar can expect to participate in a programme that combines:

Professional development

Training and bespoke sessions designed to support the development of future leaders.

Networking

Peer-to-peer interaction with other young professionals and engagement with people from different sectors.

Agricultural exposure

Opportunities to explore both supply chains and primary production.

Conference participation

CONCLUSION
